about: The roster of the Flagships tab of the Wine Atlas (codex58), wave one: 43 classic regions in 51 groups of five producers, each with the one flagship wine a sommelier is expected to know. A group is keyed by key, titled as the page heads it, tied to its region record (region, a slug of REGIONS.regions) and its country (country, the region's sheet key in REGIONS.countries), and written by its chunk. A pick is keyed by key (unique in the plan, the seed of the record's frozen id), names the producer as the house writes it, its WINE_PRODUCERS id where the library holds the house (producerId, empty when it does not), the flagship wine (the record's wine.name holds these words, and may add the Prädikat or the style the label prints), why a sommelier is expected to know it, and, where the spec agent was unsure, a note of what the author must confirm. An author may propose a swap only with a reason and the checker's agreement: it is recorded in the group's swaps (from, to, why, agreed) and the pick replaced in the same commit. schema.cjs holds every rule; build-flagships.cjs --plan proves this file against the app. Wave two follows wave one's 51 groups in the same form: the other region records the owner chose, one group of five each, keyed by its region slug and headed as its region page is, merged from the nine lanes of plan-w2/ (kept as the record) in three batches that each ship whole once built names them, A (France, Italy, Spain, Portugal), B (Germany, Austria, Hungary, Greece) and C (the New York sheet, Argentina, Chile, Australia, New Zealand, South Africa), each group carrying its batch and its chunk of wave two (w1 on, three groups a chunk in plan order, never two batches in one); a region whose lane could not source five houses waits in plan-w2/ and joins the plan only when five are sourced, since a group never ships short.

picks.why: Reims house of 1843: a multi vintage blend fermented in small old casks and built on a deep library of reserve wines, the house's own reason for being.
Épernay house of 1743; its vintage prestige cuvée, named for the Benedictine cellarer of Hautvillers, is the Champagne name a guest knows by heart.
picks.note: Teach Dom Pérignon as Moët & Chandon's prestige cuvée, made at Épernay; say how it is presented today only in words that do not age.

picks.why: Reims house of 1776; Cristal was made for Tsar Alexander II in 1876 and comes in clear glass with a flat bottom.
Aÿ family house of 1829, Pinot Noir led and partly fermented in old oak; La Grande Année is its vintage wine, aged under cork before disgorging.
Avize grower who fermented in barrel and kept a perpetual reserve; Substance, a Blanc de Blancs drawn from that reserve, made the grower movement's name. The one grower of the five.
Chablis family domaine of 1948 whose Grand Cru and Premier Cru wines, raised in old barrels, are cellared for decades.
Raveneau's kin in method: old barrels and long lives; Les Preuses is its Grand Cru on the slope's upper reaches.
picks.note: Confirm Les Preuses or Les Clos as the house's flagship and say why.

picks.wine: Chablis Grand Cru Bougros Côte Bouguerots
picks.why: A large holder of Grand Cru vines since 1959; Côte Bouguerots is the steep slope within Bougros.

picks.wine: Chablis Premier Cru Montée de Tonnerre
picks.why: The steel tank school of Chablis, with no oak since the 1960s; Montée de Tonnerre is its signature Premier Cru.
The cooperative of 1923; Château Grenouilles is its Grand Cru from Grenouilles, the smallest of the seven climats.
Vosne-Romanée domaine named in 1869 for its monopole, the vineyard the Prince de Conti bought in 1760.
Gevrey-Chambertin domaine built by Armand Rousseau from the early twentieth century, among the first in Burgundy to bottle its own wine.
Chambolle-Musigny domaine held by one family by descent since the fifteenth century; its Musigny comes from the larger part of the Grand Cru.
Chambolle-Musigny domaine of 1924; Bonnes-Mares from both the red and the white soils of the Chambolle side.
Morey-Saint-Denis Grand Cru monopole walled by Cistercian nuns, held by few owners since 1141.
Puligny-Montrachet family domaine and a biodynamic pioneer; Chevalier-Montrachet lies on the stony slope above Le Montrachet.
picks.note: Confirm Chevalier-Montrachet against Les Pucelles as the wine the house leads with.

picks.why: Meursault domaine founded by Jules Lafon in the 1890s; Les Perrières is the village's stoniest Premier Cru.
Meursault family domaine whose Corton-Charlemagne, made in very small quantity, is the rarest bottle a list may hold from it.

picks.wine: Volnay Premier Cru Clos des Ducs
picks.why: Volnay domaine whose Marquis fought fraud and championed estate bottling in the 1920s and 1930s; Clos des Ducs is its monopole.

picks.wine: Beaune Premier Cru Grèves Vigne de l'Enfant Jésus
picks.why: Beaune house of 1731; its monopole parcel in Grèves takes its name from the Carmelite nuns' devotion to the Infant Jesus.

groups.title: The Left Bank, the Médoc and Graves

picks.why: Pauillac, first of the first growths in the 1855 list; bought by Baron James de Rothschild in 1868.
Pauillac first growth by the Gironde, named for a fortified tower of the Hundred Years War; Les Forts de Latour is the second wine.
The first growth of the Margaux appellation, with a neoclassical château finished in 1815 and a white wine of its own, Pavillon Blanc.
Pessac-Léognan, the one Graves estate among the 1855 first growths, named in London by Samuel Pepys in 1663.
Pauillac, promoted to first growth in 1973, the one promotion in the 1855 list; an artist paints the label each vintage.

groups.title: The Right Bank, Saint-Émilion and Pomerol

picks.why: Pomerol Merlot on a button of blue clay, made famous after the Second World War by Madame Loubat and the Moueix family.
Pomerol's tiny estate of 1979, Merlot alone from a few rows, the first wine called a vin de garage.
Saint-Émilion estate on the Pomerol border, Cabernet Franc led on gravel and clay; the 1947 is a vintage of history.
Saint-Émilion côte estate on limestone named for the Roman poet Ausonius, Cabernet Franc led.
Saint-Émilion estate on gravel with an unusual share of Cabernet Sauvignon; promoted to Premier Grand Cru Classé A in 2022.
The one Premier Cru Supérieur of 1855, held by the Lur Saluces family from 1785 to 1999.
Barsac Premier Cru on red sand over limestone, Sémillon alone.
Barsac Premier Cru around a thirteenth century tower; its Cuvée Madame is made only in rare years.
Preignac Premier Cru beside Yquem, rich and Sémillon led, its gardens laid out in the seventeenth century manner.
Preignac estate that ages its Sauternes for many years in concrete vats before release, outside the 1855 list.
Ampuis house of 1946; La Mouline, first made in 1966, opened the single vineyard Côte-Rôtie of the three La La wines.
Tain house of 1834, its Hermitage named for the chapel on the hill; the 1961 is a vintage of history.
Mauves family in wine since 1481 by its own account; its Hermitage rouge blends parcels across the hill.
The Cornas family domaine that kept old vine, whole bunch Syrah alive in the appellation.
The family credited with keeping Condrieu alive when it was nearly abandoned; Coteau de Vernon is its oldest Viognier.
Courthézon estate of the Perrin family, all thirteen grapes planted, with an unusual share of Mourvèdre.
Sandy, north facing estate of old Grenache, a Châteauneuf of perfume rather than power.
Named for the Chappe telegraph tower on the plateau of La Crau, its rolled stones; the Brunier family since 1891.
Avril family estate whose single red blends parcels from across the appellation.
Gigondas estate with Roman era vats cut in the rock: the appellation beside Châteauneuf, under the Dentelles.
picks.note: Confirm the bottling: the estate's Gigondas or a named lieu-dit.

picks.why: Vouvray estate of 1928 whose three vineyards are made dry, medium dry or sweet as the year allows.
picks.note: Confirm Le Haut-Lieu, Le Mont or Clos du Bourg as the house's flagship.

picks.why: Savennières Chenin monopole planted by Cistercian monks in 1130, a biodynamic pioneer and an appellation of its own.
Pouilly-Fumé domaine whose founder raised the appellation's ambition; Silex comes from flint soils.
Chacé domaine of the Foucault family, Cabernet Franc in old barrels; Le Bourg is its old vine parcel.
Sancerre family in wine since 1513 by its own account; La Moussière is its domaine Sauvignon Blanc.

picks.why: Ribeauvillé house of 1626; Clos Sainte Hune, a family plot within Grand Cru Rosacker, carries no Grand Cru name on its label.

picks.wine: Riesling Rangen de Thann Clos Saint Urbain
picks.why: Turckheim domaine of 1959; Clos Saint Urbain lies on the volcanic slope of the Rangen, Alsace's southernmost Grand Cru.

picks.wine: Riesling Grand Cru Schlossberg Cuvée Sainte Catherine

Bergheim domaine that bottles field blends of co-planted grapes under the Grand Cru's name alone.
Villié-Morgon domaine whose founder led the natural wine Gang of Four, with little or no sulphur.
Villié-Morgon grower of the Gang of Four; Côte du Py is Morgon's hill of decomposed blue schist.
Odenas estate of 1877 on the volcanic slopes of Mont Brouilly.
Romanèche-Thorins estate that ages Moulin-à-Vent in barrel, climat by climat, as Burgundy does.
The négociant of Romanèche-Thorins who made the third Thursday of November a release the world waits for.
Barbaresco house of 1859 that carried the appellation abroad; its Barbaresco blends parcels around the village.
Monforte d'Alba house of 1908; Monfortino is a long macerated Riserva made only in strong years and aged for years in large casks.
Barolo village house of 1919 that blends several crus into one traditional Barolo, as the old houses did.

picks.wine: Barolo Le Rocche del Falletto Riserva
picks.why: Neive house whose Riserve wear a red label; Falletto in Serralunga is its own vineyard.
The cooperative of 1958, revived from a forerunner of 1894, whose village Barbaresco and single vineyard Riserve teach the appellation.
Florentine family in wine since 1385; Tignanello, first released from the 1971 vintage, led the Super Tuscan movement.
Brolio castle family; Baron Bettino Ricasoli set down a recipe for Chianti in 1872.
Panzano estate in the Conca d'Oro; Flaccianello is Sangiovese alone from the estate.
Radda estate of 1967 whose Sangiovese alone stood outside the Chianti rules from 1977.
Barberino Tavarnelle estate whose Sangiovese alone, Cepparello, first made in 1980, stood outside the Chianti rules.
Tenuta Greppo, where the Biondi Santi family selected Sangiovese and bottled the first Brunello in the nineteenth century.
Sant'Angelo in Colle estate of the nineteenth century, among the early Brunello houses.

picks.wine: Poggio all'Oro Brunello di Montalcino Riserva
picks.why: Estate of 1978 founded by an American importing family that took Brunello to a wide market abroad.
Estate of 1971 whose modern Brunello from the Tenuta Nuova vineyard drew new attention to the south east of the hill.
Estate of 1972 whose founder left the Brunello denomination after vandals emptied his casks in 2012.

picks.why: The Incisa della Rocchetta family's Cabernet, first sold from the 1968 vintage; Bolgheri Sassicaia became a DOC of its own in 2013.
Bolgheri estate of 1981 founded by a younger son of the Antinori family; its blend is led by Cabernet Sauvignon and Merlot.
The second estate to plant for fine wine in Bolgheri, in 1977, high on the hills of Castagneto Carducci.
Bolgheri estate of 1983 whose Paleo Rosso became Cabernet Franc alone.
Suvereto estate of 1984 whose Merlot, Redigaffi, carried the coast's name south of Bolgheri.

picks.why: Negrar house whose founder set the slow, long aged model for Amarone, released late.

Valpolicella house whose Campofiorin, from the 1964 vintage, gave the ripasso style its model.
Soave house of 1880, the first to bottle a single vineyard Soave, Calvarino, in 1971.
Valdobbiadene family whose Cartizze comes from the steep hill at the head of the Prosecco Superiore ladder.
Farra d'Isonzo house whose Vintage Tunina, a white blend first made in 1975, named a Friulian style.

Oslavia estate that turned to buried Georgian clay amphorae and long skin contact, the model of orange wine.

Mezzolombardo estate that rescued Teroldego by selection in the Campo Rotaliano; Granato is its long lived red.

Sorbo Serpico estate of 1986 that brought modern cellar work to Irpinia's whites and reds.

Cellole estate that revived the ancient Falernian vineyard; Vigna Camarato is its Aglianico led red.

La Horra estate of 1995 whose first vintage made Ribera a name abroad.
Pesquera de Duero house of 1972 that, beside Vega Sicilia, put Ribera on wine lists abroad.
Peñafiel winery of 1927 that gave its old name, Ribera Duero, to the region in 1982 and became Protos, the Greek for first.

Jerez house whose Inocente is a single vineyard Fino from Macharnudo, fermented in cask and aged long under flor.

picks.why: The Peyraud family estate at Le Plan du Castellet that built Bandol's name on Mourvèdre; La Tourtine, its structured parcel red from a windswept slope by Le Castellet, is the wine that teaches Bandol rouge.

Merge read, from memory and unsourced: lists pour the domaine's Bandol rosé and its classic Bandol rouge more often than La Tourtine; if the house's own pages or two sources call either the wine it is known by, propose the swap with the checker.

picks.why: The Meyreuil estate of one family whose own recognition by the INAO grew into the small Palette appellation; its white, raised long in small oak foudres and then barrels from very old vines, is the wine of the appellation.
picks.note: Say the estate's share of Palette only in words that do not age; confirm the white's grapes (Clairette leading, by the library) and its cellars from the estate's page or two sources.

picks.why: The Alpilles estate planted on cleared limestone scrub from 1973, whose red of Cabernet Sauvignon and Syrah broke the Baux-de-Provence rule on Cabernet and is sold as IGP Alpilles.

picks.why: The house begun in 1896 by an Alsatian agricultural engineer who settled in Provence and bought Château de Selle in 1912, which helped carry Provence rosé onto wine lists; the rosé of Château de Selle, in the house's curved bottle, is the wine to know.
picks.note: Confirm the label words (Château de Selle, Cœur de Grain) and the date and story of the curved bottle in two sources; give the founder's dates from two sources; Clos Mireille and Château Romassan go in others; later ownership is history, dated.

picks.why: The La Motte-en-Provence estate behind Whispering Angel, the Côtes de Provence rosé guests ask for by name; Garrus, its oak-fermented rosé, is the estate's other face.

picks.why: The Aniane estate of the early 1970s whose Cabernet Sauvignon-led red, first made with the 1978 vintage on soil the estate calls glacial in origin, argued that the Languedoc could make wine to age, sold outside the appellations.

picks.producer: Domaine de la Grange des Pères
picks.why: Aniane's other estate, planted from the late 1980s and first made in 1992, whose red of Syrah, Mourvèdre and Cabernet Sauvignon is aged long in barrel and sold as IGP Pays d'Hérault.
picks.note: The founder died in 2021 and his dates are not settled, so he is described, never named; his brother, who carried the domaine on, is living and is never named. Confirm the grapes in words and the IGP on the label; the white goes in others.

picks.why: The Jonquières estate of 1985, counted among the pioneers of the Languedoc's revival, in the hills that became the Terrasses du Larzac appellation; Autour de Jonquières, its principal red, blends Mourvèdre, Carignan and Syrah from parcels around the village.
picks.note: The founder is living and is never named; confirm the red's grapes and the appellation on its label (Terrasses du Larzac, older vintages Coteaux du Languedoc) in two sources.

picks.why: The Calce estate on limestone and schist in the Agly valley, counted among the pioneers of dry Roussillon; Muntada, its red of old Grenache and of Carignan more than a century old, is the estate's flagship.
picks.note: The family is living and is never named; confirm Muntada's grapes and its label (IGP Côtes Catalanes or Côtes du Roussillon Villages) in the vintages taught; Coume Gineste goes in others.

picks.why: The Maury estate known for vin doux naturel of Grenache left first in glass bonbonnes in the sun and then for decades in large oak foudres; the twenty year old shows that oxidative style in full.
picks.note: The estate's own range lists its aged Maury as 20, 30 and 40 Ans d'Âge and no 10, so the twenty year old took the ten's place by the swap of 2026-11-14; the Vintage and the Cuvée Spéciale 10 Ans d'Âge go in others.

picks.why: The Château-Chalon family estate whose vin jaune, Savagnin aged untopped under its veil of yeast and released in the 62 cl clavelin, is the wine a sommelier is taught to place.
picks.note: Confirm the family's dates before naming anyone; give the vin jaune rule from the appellation text (sixty months untopped by the region record); the Côtes du Jura Blanc goes in others.

picks.why: The Pupillin estate whose Ploussard, a pale red made with little or no added sulphur, became a bottle the natural wine movement looks to; it teaches the Jura's own red grape.
picks.note: The grower whose name the house bears and his successor are living: name neither in prose, say the founder and his successor. Confirm the label and the sulphur custom in two sources.

picks.why: The Montigny-lès-Arsures family estate that makes every Jura style; Les Bruyères, a topped-up, single-vineyard Chardonnay, shows the fresh idiom beside the oxidative one.
picks.note: The son who runs it is living and is never named; confirm Les Bruyères's soil and élevage and any biodynamic farming with its year in two sources; the vin jaune and the Crémant go in others.

picks.why: The historic château estate of the Côtes du Jura at Arlay, long a reference for vin jaune and vin de paille; its vin de paille, from grapes dried for months before pressing, is the sweet face of the region.
picks.note: Confirm the label (Côtes du Jura Vin de Paille), its grapes and the drying from the estate or two sources; the family is living and is never named; the vin jaune goes in others.

picks.why: The Arbois estate founded in 2012 by a family of Volnay, bottling Savagnin topped up, beside its vin jaune; the ouillé Savagnin shows the grape without the veil.
picks.note: Name the Volnay family by its domaine, never its living members (one is in people.json); say which vines it took on only from two sources; the vin jaune goes in others.

picks.why: A family estate at Arbin in the Combe de Savoie, wound down in the early 2020s, whose Mondeuse from the cru of Arbin is a clear way to teach Savoie's own red grape.

Its leased Arbin vines had passed to Domaine des Ardoisières by 2024; a swap to a working house of Arbin was proposed and refused on 2026-11-14, as reviews/check-savoie.json records, since the record tells the end of the house as history and its bottles stay on lists.

picks.why: The estate begun in 1998 to replant the abandoned schist slopes of Cevins in the Tarentaise, whose Cevins wines are bottled as IGP Vin des Allobroges; Quartz, its Altesse, is the white to know.

picks.why: A family estate at Aimavigne in Jongieux at the foot of the Marestel slope, known for long-lived Altesse from the cru; its Marestel shows what the grape becomes with age.

picks.why: A family estate at Mérignat in the Bugey known for Cerdon, the pink, sweetish sparkling wine of Gamay and Poulsard made by the ancestral method, its fermentation finished in the bottle.

picks.why: The Vire-sur-Lot estate whose Le Cèdre, Malbec alone from limestone scree and the high terraces above the Lot, aged about two years in large oak, teaches what modern Cahors is.

The estate's range lists Montus Prestige and Montus XL as separate cuvées, so XL goes in others; the buyer of 1980 is living and is never named.

picks.why: The Gaillac family estate that keeps the old local grapes in the vineyard; its Mauzac Nature, sparkling by the ancestral method with its fermentation finished in bottle, teaches the old Gaillac way with bubbles.

picks.why: The Patrimonio family estate on limestone whose Vermentino from the Carco parcel shows how long the island's white can live.

Carco is Vermentinu from one parcel, planted in 1987; since the estate was shared around 2014 Grotte di Sole is bottled by the elder son under his own name, so it does not go in others, and the Bianco Gentile does.

picks.why: The Taravo valley estate in the Ajaccio country, farmed biodynamically since 2000, that keeps a collection of the island's old grapes; Faustine, its red of Sciaccarellu with some Niellucciu, has been labelled Vin de France since the house took its wines out of the appellations.
picks.note: Faustine was sold as Ajaccio in earlier vintages; the Cuvées Collection go in others. The general of the Revolution among the family's historic figures is described, never named, since his birth year is 1770 or 1771 by source and his name is also the living head's; the living family is never named.

picks.why: An estate at Rogliano at the northern tip of Cap Corse, on schist, known for its Vermentino and its Muscat du Cap Corse, the vin doux naturel of Muscat à Petits Grains.
picks.note: The Muscat is Muscatellu, by the Hachette guide and the Wine Scholar Guild, which calls it the house's flagship; the dry white, Corse Coteaux du Cap Corse, goes in others; the family is living and is never named.

picks.why: A family estate of Patrimonio on limestone, a clear example of Nielluccio, the grape DNA ties to Sangiovese, in the island's northern appellation.

Domaine Leccia is the family estate, not Domaine d'E Croce, which the brother founded apart in 2004 or 2005; the living family is never named.

picks.why: Erbusco house of 1968, exacting and given to long lees ageing; its vintage Riserva, named for the founder's mother, about eight years on its lees and with no dosage since the 2008 vintage, is the wine the library already teaches.

The house prints Annamaria Clementi with the designation Franciacorta Riserva; the founder's mother is described, for want of her birth year in two sources, and the founder is living and is never named.

picks.why: Erbusco house of 1977 whose base wines ferment partly in small oak; its vintage Satèn, Chardonnay alone at lower pressure, teaches the type whose name the Franciacorta consortium registered in 1995.
picks.note: The house's prestige Riserva carries its living founder's name, so the Satèn is taught. The label is Franciacorta Satèn with the vintage, Chardonnay alone on the house's sheets; the library's Franciacorta Gran Cuvée Satèn is an older name. No source read sets Alma, the non vintage Gran Cuvée, at the head of the range, so no swap was proposed, as reviews/check-lombardy.json records.

picks.why: Chiuro house of 1897 whose cellars lie in the fifteenth century palace of the Quadrio family there; Sfursat 5 Stelle is the dried grape Nebbiolo the library teaches Sforzato di Valtellina with.
picks.note: The house heads the wine Sfursat 5 Stelle, Sforzato di Valtellina DOCG; the library's Sfursat di Valtellina 5 Stelle and the region record's 5 Stelle Sfursat are other orders. No source read calls the house the valley's largest, so the why no longer does; the year it passed to the Gruppo Italiano Vini, 1986 or the end of the 1970s, stays open.

picks.why: Sondrio family house of the Valtellina terraces, begun again in 1984, with long macerations, large casks of chestnut and oak and late release; Rocce Rosse is its Valtellina Superiore Sassella Riserva.
picks.note: Rocce Rosse is still made as a Sassella Riserva in the years the family judges exceptional and is held for years in cask and bottle. The refounder died in 2004 by the sources read and is described; his children run the house, are living and are never named.

picks.why: Sirmione family estate on the south shore of Lake Garda, there since 1939 by its own account; I Frati is its Lugana of Turbiana, the white side of the region.
picks.note: 1939 stands on the house's pages, the Valpolicella consortium's producer page and a guide; the label is Lugana I Frati, Turbiana alone; Brolettino, the house's Lugana aged in barriques, is in others. The grower's living children are never named.

picks.why: Montefalco estate of 1971 that made dry Sagrantino a modern wine through clonal work with the University of Milan; 25 Anni is the bottling that carried Sagrantino abroad.
picks.note: 25 Anni was first made with the 1993 vintage, its name the estate's twenty fifth year. The founder died in 2026 and is named with his death and his age; his son, who turned the estate towards research, is living and is never named.

picks.why: Small Montefalco family estate of long macerations, wild yeasts, no fining or filtering and late release; Pagliaro is its single vineyard Montefalco Sagrantino, the natural wine reference of the zone.
picks.note: The house keeps its name; the father whose name it carries is listed in people.json as a precaution, his status not settled, and no living member of the family is named in prose. Labels print Montefalco Sagrantino and Sagrantino di Montefalco, and the record teaches both.

picks.why: The Torgiano house that won the village a DOC in 1968 and its Rosso Riserva a DOCG in 1990; Rubesco Riserva Vigna Monticchio is the wine of that DOCG.
picks.note: The house prints Rubesco Riserva Vigna Monticchio, the order the record follows. The founder carries his death alone (1999), for want of a birth year in two sources; his wife is described, and his living daughters are never named.

picks.why: The Antinori family's castle estate near Orvieto, with its own label; Cervaro della Sala, Chardonnay fermented in barrique with a little Grechetto fermented apart in steel, is the Umbrian white a sommelier meets.
picks.note: Wave one holds Marchesi Antinori in Chianti Classico with Tignanello; this is the family's Umbrian estate, its own home and a different wine. The estate gives 1940 for the family's purchase and 1985 for the first Cervaro; the winemaker who came in 1979 is living and is never named.

picks.why: Organic family estate above Lake Corbara in the Orvieto Classico zone; Calcaia is its sweet Orvieto of noble rot, the style the lake's autumn mists allow.
picks.note: No source read gives 1981: one gives 1986 for the house's first Muffa Nobile and another 1991 for the first Calcaia, so the record tells no first vintage. The label reads Orvieto Classico Superiore Muffa Nobile Calcaia; the founder's grandsons are living and are never named.

picks.why: Loreto Aprutino estate of old pergola vines that bottles only in the years it accepts; its Trebbiano d'Abruzzo is the white the library teaches as proof the grape can age.
picks.note: The library also holds the wine as w-trebbiano-valentini, and the record builds on both. The old pergola vines stand on Vinous and two merchants' pages and are not yet told in the record; no living member of the family is named.

picks.why: Torano Nuovo house of 1964 in the Teramo hills, unfiltered and long held in bottle, its old vintages decanted by hand before release; its Montepulciano d'Abruzzo is the flagship.
picks.note: The house keeps its founder's name; he died on 28 July 2026 at 94 and is named with his dates (1932 to 2026). His daughters and granddaughters are living and are never named.

picks.why: San Martino sulla Marrucina house of 1981 that took polished, oak aged Montepulciano d'Abruzzo abroad; Villa Gemma Riserva is its flagship and the modern pole of the region.
picks.note: The house's sheets give Villa Gemma Montepulciano d'Abruzzo DOC Riserva. The founder carries his death alone (2008), his age at death 52 or 53 by source; his partner and his daughter are living and are never named, nor are the house's two wines that carry the partner's name.

picks.why: House of 1890, begun at Ripatransone in the Marche and at Controguerra in the Teramo hills since 1960, that worked for the Colline Teramane DOCG; Zanna is its long aged Montepulciano Riserva.
picks.note: 1890 and the label (Montepulciano d'Abruzzo Colline Teramane Riserva) are confirmed; Zanna's first vintage is still in no source. The founder of 1890 shares his name with a living descendant, so he is described, and the living family is never named.

picks.why: Ofena estate in the hot basin under the Gran Sasso; Piè delle Vigne, Montepulciano made pink, is its Cerasuolo d'Abruzzo, the region's deep coloured rosato.
picks.note: The house names no flagship and one merchant names the Montepulciano Tonì; the Cerasuolo is kept so the group holds the rosato. Labels read Cerasuolo d'Abruzzo DOC, and Cerasuolo d'Abruzzo Superiore Terre Aquilane DOC for the 2024, so the record prints Cerasuolo d'Abruzzo alone; the daughter who runs the estate is living and is never named.

picks.why: Manduria estate of 2004 working old alberello Primitivo vines around Manduria and Sava; Es, labelled Primitivo di Manduria DOC in its early vintages and Salento IGT in later ones, argued that Primitivo could be fine as well as big.
picks.note: The house carries its living founder's name: the house is named, and allowed as the house in its own record, while the founder and his wife are listed in people.json and never named in prose. The library's Primitivo di Manduria DOC holds for the early vintages of Es only, as reviews/check-puglia.json records.

picks.why: Castel del Monte house of 1950 that championed Nero di Troia; Il Falcone, Nero di Troia with Montepulciano, is the Riserva that carried the grape and the DOCG of 2011.
picks.note: The seat at Andria is confirmed, and the label reads Il Falcone, Castel del Monte Rosso Riserva DOCG, for the vintages since 2011, a Riserva of the Castel del Monte DOC before. The library's 1950 stands beside the house's late 1940s, and the patriarch's purchase of 1921 is the house's account; the founder is undated and described, and his son and grandsons are living and never named.

picks.why: Salice Salentino house dating its origins to 1665; Five Roses, a rosato of Negroamaro with a little Malvasia Nera, bottled from 1943, is the one the house tells as the first rosé bottled and sold in Italy.
picks.note: 1665 and 1943 are the house's own dates, with the Drinks Business and merchants beside them, and the first bottled rosé is told as the house's claim throughout. The couple who began bottling in 1925 are undated and described.

picks.why: Guagnano estate of the Salento whose founder died in 1999; Patriglione, Negroamaro picked late from old bush vines with some bunches shrivelled on the vine, first made in 1975, became the house's flagship.
picks.note: The first Patriglione is the 1975 on the house's page and a Veronelli reprint; Cosimo Taurino keeps his death of 1999 alone, for want of a birth year in two sources. The oenologist he worked with is described, not named, and his children are living and never named. The story of a forgotten cask rests on one importer and is not told.

picks.why: Estate between Acquaviva delle Fonti and Gioia del Colle with a cellar dug into the limestone; its numbered Gioia del Colle Primitivo shows the fresher side of the grape on the Murge.
picks.note: A thin pick, kept under the thin region rule. The house names the wine Polvanera 16 and merchants Gioia del Colle DOC Primitivo 16 Vigneto San Benedetto, so the plan's words stand in the name; no source read calls the 16 or the 17 the flagship, and the record treats the 16 as a wine the house is known by. What the numbers mean is unsettled, and the founding year is in dispute, so founded is empty; the founder and his father are never named. Cantine San Marzano's Sessantanni stays the alternative, untested.

swaps.why: the house's own pages put the wine named Capichera, made since 1980, first, as its iconic wine and its first; house and key kept

picks.why: Serdiana estate of 1938; Turriga, a Cannonau led barrique blend first harvested in 1988 and released in 1991, is the Sardinian red a candidate is expected to name.
picks.note: The first harvest of 1988, the release of 1991, the blend of Cannonau with Carignano, Bovale Sardo and Malvasia Nera and the label Isola dei Nuraghi IGT are confirmed. The founder (1906 to 2009) shares his name with a living grandson, so the record describes him, and the third generation is never named.

picks.why: Alghero estate founded in 1899 by two Piedmontese on reclaimed land, first as a nursery of young vines grafted on American rootstocks; Terre Bianche is its Torbato, a rare white grape the house, by its own account, brought back.
picks.note: The record teaches Terre Bianche Cuvée 161, the house's fullest Torbato, kept beside a plain Terre Bianche; Anghelu Ruju and Marchese di Villamarina are in others. The claim that the house long grew Torbato almost alone rests on one source and is not told; the two founders are undated and described.

picks.why: Cabras family house of 1898 on the Oristano gulf; Antico Gregori, born of the family's long reserves and aged for decades in part filled casks under flor, is the Vernaccia di Oristano the library teaches.
picks.note: Recent releases of Antico Gregori carry a vintage, each aged for decades, and the 1991 was freshened with much older Vernaccia; the label reads Vernaccia di Oristano DOC Riserva. The library's blend of very old reserves holds for the older bottlings; 1898, on the house's history page and in the library, stands against 1895 on the house's own Vernaccia page, open for the integrator. The fourth generation is living and never named.

picks.why: The Sulcis co-operative and the voice of its zone; Terre Brune, first made in 1984, turned old ungrafted Carignano on sand into a serious Carignano del Sulcis Superiore.
picks.note: 1984 for the first Terre Brune and Carignano with about a twentieth of Bovaleddu are confirmed; Giacomo Tachis came to the co-operative in the 1980s by its own pages, his first year there open. The long serving president and the oenologist are living and never named.

picks.why: Arzachena estate in the granite of the Gallura that made Vermentino a wine of weight and ageing, long labelled outside the DOCG; the wine named Capichera, made since 1980, is the one the house puts first, with the barrique aged VT beside it.
picks.note: The house's own pages call the wine named Capichera its first and the one it puts first, so it took the VT's place by the swap of 2026-11-14, house and key kept; the VT Vendemmia Tardiva, made since 1990 and dry despite its name, leads the others. Its labels read Isola dei Nuraghi IGT until the 2024 vintage, when the house's pages give Vermentino di Gallura Superiore DOCG, open for the integrator. The family is never named, nor the estate's reported buyer.

picks.why: Modena house of 1860 and a reference for dry Lambrusco; Vecchia Modena Premium is its pale, sharp Lambrusco di Sorbara, the side of the family the library sets against Grasparossa.
picks.note: The label is Vecchia Modena Premium, later ones adding Mention Honorable, Lambrusco di Sorbara DOC, made in a sealed tank by the Charmat method on the house's sheet and an importer's. The Premium of 2000 is the house's account (an importer gives 2001), and one importer speaks of a Vecchia Modena Nero from the 2023 vintage, for the integrator. The founder is undated and named only as the house; his descendants of the estate branch are living and never named.

picks.why: Reggio Emilia family house whose dry Concerto, Lambrusco Salamino of its own Tenuta La Rampata first made in 1993, helped restore the name of dry Lambrusco on the Reggio side.
picks.note: The house dates itself to 1890, where a sister house's history and the Strada dei Vini differ, open in the record; Concerto is Lambrusco Salamino of La Rampata first made in 1993, 1994 in one account, and every claim of a first is left out. The founder and his son are undated and described, and the fourth and fifth generations are living and never named.

picks.why: Sorbara family estate of 1926 in the Cristo di Sorbara; Radice is its pale Lambrusco di Sorbara refermented in bottle and never disgorged, the old way of the countryside.
picks.note: 1926 stands on a Dutch merchant's page and in the family's own centenary of 2026. Leclisse, given its sparkle in tank, is the house's other Sorbara; no source read puts it on the oldest vines, so the note no longer does. The founder is undated and described, and the family who run the estate are living and never named.

picks.why: Faenza estate whose Scacco Matto, a botrytised Albana passito, makes the case for Albana di Romagna, the first white DOCG of Italy in 1987.
picks.note: 1966 for the founding stands on the house, the Gazzetta di Parma and Bibenda, against the library's empty field; Scacco Matto was first made in 1987, and the label reads Romagna Albana Passito DOCG, Albana di Romagna Passito on older bottles. The founder is undated and described, and his granddaughter, who took the estate in hand in 1987, and her brother are living and never named.

picks.why: Historic estate of the Colli Piacentini at Rivergaro; Ageno, Malvasia di Candia Aromatica long on its skins, with Ortrugo and Trebbiano beside it in earlier vintages and alone in later ones, is the wine the house is known by abroad and an orange wine of Emilia.
picks.note: Rivergaro in the Val Trebbiola is confirmed. The founder, a lawyer of the second half of the nineteenth century whose surname the wine carries, has no dates in any source read, so founded is empty and he is described; the label reads Emilia IGT or Vino Bianco by vintage, the year of the change open. Some importers call Macchiona the flagship red. The family's daughter who runs the estate and its cellar master are living and never named.

picks.why: Castelli di Jesi estate, a family's for generations until its sale of 2024, whose Villa Bucci Riserva, matured in large old casks of Slavonian oak, makes the case for Verdicchio as a white to age.
picks.note: The label reads Castelli di Jesi Verdicchio Riserva Classico, a DOCG, from 2010, and Verdicchio dei Castelli di Jesi DOC before, as the record has it; the why's family estate is history since the sale of July 2024. Ampelio Bucci is named with his death in 2025 at 89; the consultant oenologist and the buyers of 2024 are described, never named, the buyers listed in people.json. The months in cask (12 to 18) and the cask sizes vary by vintage and source, so the record gives what every listing allows.

picks.why: Matelica estate in the landlocked upper valley; Mirum is its Verdicchio di Matelica Riserva, the tighter, slower inland Verdicchio the library sets against Jesi.
picks.note: Mirum is Verdicchio alone by the house's sheet and a merchant, no source read tying Chardonnay to it, first made in 1988 and dedicated to the founder; the house dates itself to 1966, where the library leaves the year empty, as reviews/check-marche.json records. The founder, his status unsettled, and his son, who joined in 1982, are described, never named, and listed in people.json.

picks.why: Castelplanio house whose amphora shaped bottle, chosen by a design competition of 1953, carried Verdicchio abroad; Titulus is the Verdicchio dei Castelli di Jesi Classico that wears it.
picks.note: The competition of 1953 stands on the house and three secondary accounts, one dating the design to 1954, and the move to Castelplanio in 1956 on three secondary accounts and no page of the house's; the house began at Cupramontana in 1949. The Angelini family's takeover is told without its year; the industrialist and the architect, their status unsettled, are described, never named, and listed in people.json as precautions, as is the film star of the bottle's American nickname.

picks.why: Osimo house of the Conero and the Castelli di Jesi; Cùmaro, Montepulciano from a vineyard on the edge of Osimo, inland of Monte Conero, is its Conero Riserva, the red side of the Marche.
picks.note: The seat at Osimo from 1969, a year after the takeover of 1968, the founding of 1957 at Cupramontana and Cùmaro's first vintage of 1985 as Conero Riserva DOCG are confirmed; the why no longer puts the vineyard on the slopes of the headland. 1959 against 1968 for the partners' arrival and whether the Abruzzo estate of 2001 was bought are open. The founder, the man and his son in law of 1968 and the son in law's son are described, never named, and listed in people.json. Campo San Giorgio, the house's single vineyard Conero Riserva, is not taught.

picks.why: Ascoli Piceno house of the southern Marche, known for the Piceno reds and the Offida whites; Roggio del Filare, Montepulciano with Sangiovese, is its Rosso Piceno Superiore.
picks.note: Founded in 1984 at Ascoli Piceno; Roggio del Filare is about seven tenths Montepulciano with Sangiovese by the house's sheets (two listings give half and all Montepulciano), first made from the 1993 vintage and labelled Rosso Piceno Superiore DOC. Brecciarolo's first year (1984 or 1986 by the house's two pages), whether the Superiore's year of ageing must be spent in wood, and thirteen or fourteen communes are open. The two founders and the manager of 2005 are living, never named, and listed in people.json. The Offida Pecorino stays the white alternative, untested.

picks.why: Growers' co-operative at Groppo above Manarola and the voice of the cliffs, gathering grapes from many small terraces; its Cinque Terre Sciacchetrà is the sweet wine of dried Bosco, Albarola and Vermentino.
picks.note: Founded in 1973, the year of the DOC, by the LEI register and the Ministry's page; the co-operative writes its name as Agricoltura di Riomaggiore, Manarola, Corniglia, Vernazza e Monterosso and bottles as Cantina Cinque Terre. The label reads Cinque Terre Sciacchetrà DOC, Bosco the great majority with a little Albarola and Vermentino. The drying, naturally on racks for about two months by the house, is told without sun or shade; Bosco's least share by the decree is open.

picks.why: Dolceacqua estate whose Rossese vines go back to 1870 by the family's account; Bricco Arcagna, from the top of the Arcagna hill, is its Rossese di Dolceacqua.
picks.note: 1870 is the house's own date, told as its account. Labels read Rossese di Dolceacqua, the DOC's lawful pair of names being Rossese di Dolceacqua or Dolceacqua, and no source read calls Bricco Arcagna a Superiore. Arcagna's height (the record says around 400 metres), the year the named vineyards entered the rules and the barrels are open in the record. The family who run the estate are living, never named, and listed in people.json; the forebears of 1870 are undated and described.

picks.why: Family house of the Colli di Luni on the Tuscan border, named for the Roman city of Luni; Etichetta Nera is its fuller Vermentino, given skin contact and a longer time on its lees.
picks.note: Founded in 1966 in most accounts, 1970 in one listing; the house writes Cantine Lunae, styled LVNAE, and listings print Lunae Bosoni; the label reads Colli di Luni Vermentino Etichetta Nera, first made with the 1992 vintage. The skin contact (about eight hours by the house's sheet, up to forty eight in two listings) is open. The house keeps its name, while the founder and his son are living, never named, and listed in people.json.

picks.why: Aymavilles estate founded in 1989 by a family long rooted in the valley; Cuvée Bois, a barrel fermented Chardonnay, is its flagship, with Petite Arvine and Fumin for the native grapes.
picks.note: 1989 stands on the region's page and the house. Cuvée Bois, first made with the 1995 vintage, is the wine Enocode credits with the house's name, so the pick is kept and Petite Arvine stays among the others. The family settled at Aymavilles about 1750, whence it came open (the Grenoble area or Haute-Savoie). The founder of 1989 is living and his father's status unsettled: both are described, never named, and listed in people.json.

picks.producer: Cave Mont Blanc de Morgex et La Salle
picks.wine: Blanc de Morgex et de La Salle
picks.why: The co-operative of 1983 under Mont Blanc and the voice of its sub-zone of the Valle d'Aosta DOC, making Blanc de Morgex et de La Salle from ungrafted Prié Blanc grown at up to about 1,200 metres.
picks.note: The bottling taught is the still DOC white, which the house lists among its whites under the sub-zone's name. The house writes Cave Mont Blanc de Morgex et La Salle, founded in 1983 as the Cave du Vin Blanc de Morgex et de La Salle out of the growers' association of 1971 (one account gives 1988); the why now says sub-zone, since Blanc de Morgex et de La Salle is no DOC of its own. The parish priest of 1971 is described, never named.

swaps.why: the house names its white Donna Adriana and counts it among its whites of 1993; Vigna Adriana is the older name; house and key kept

picks.why: Monte Porzio Catone house whose wines carried Frascati abroad; Vigneto Santa Teresa, a single vineyard on the volcanic hills, is its Frascati Superiore.
picks.note: The blend is Malvasia di Candia and Malvasia del Lazio, the Puntinata, with Greco by the house, Trebbiano beside them in older vintages (2004 and 2015 by two listings), the year it left the blend open; no source read gives the vineyard's first vintage. The house dates its cellars to 1958; Luna Mater is its Frascati Superiore DOCG Riserva. The manager its group names is living and never named.

picks.why: Grottaferrata estate whose first wines of 1993 followed eight years of research and the replanting of the whole estate; Donna Adriana, Viognier with Malvasia del Lazio sold as Lazio IGT, is its white, sold in its early vintages as Vigna Adriana, some labelled Frascati.
picks.note: The wine took the name Donna Adriana by the swap of 2026-11-14, house and key kept: the house names its white Donna Adriana among its whites of 1993, and Vigna Adriana is the older name of listings from 1997 to the early 2000s, some labelled Frascati. The research from 1985 (to 1992 or 1993), the replanting of 1988 to 1993 and the first wines of 1993 are confirmed, and the why no longer names the University of Milan, which one account contradicts. The year of the change of name and the early blend are open. Founded is empty, the house dating its land to 1974 and its wines to 1993. The politician who bought the land, his son and the professor are never named and listed in people.json.

picks.why: Montefiascone house of 1979 in the Est! Est!! Est!!! country; Montiano, Merlot alone first made in 1993 and labelled Lazio IGT, later IGP, is the red that drew notice to the north of the region.
picks.note: Founded in 1979 at Montefiascone by two brothers of the family; the first Montiano is the 1993, outside the DOC rules (Vino da Tavola for 1993 and 1994 in one listing), then Lazio IGT and IGP on later sheets, so the why no longer gives the IGT alone. The founders, both in people.json, and their daughters, who took the lead in 2016, are never named; the growers of the 1960s are described and listed as precautions. The year the business came to trade as Famiglia Cotarella is open.

picks.why: Family estate of the Cesanese del Piglio, its cellar on the road between Anagni and Paliano and its vines around Anagni, Acuto and Piglio; Torre del Piano, from a single vineyard at Acuto, is its Cesanese del Piglio Superiore Riserva, from the red DOCG of Lazio.
picks.note: 1921, in an importer's profile and one other account and on no page of the house's read, stays out, so founded is empty and the why no longer dates the roots; nor is the estate an Acuto one, its cellar standing between Anagni and Paliano. The vineyard (Acuto, 335 metres, planted 1986, Guyot) and the ageing (some six to eight months in barriques) rest on the house's sheets, the vessels of two merchants' accounts open. The owner is living, never named, and listed in people.json.

picks.why: Le Ferriere estate of 1967 on the reclaimed Agro Pontino, known for trials of many grapes and for reviving Bellone; Mater Matuta, Syrah with Petit Verdot, is its red, named for the goddess whose temple at ancient Satricum stood beside its vineyards.
picks.note: 1967, Syrah about 85 per cent with Petit Verdot and the temple at Satricum close to Le Ferriere are confirmed; the temple stood beside the vineyards, not on the estate, as the why had it. Mater Matuta's first vintage (the oldest seen is 2004), the French archaeologist of 1896 and which reds the trials favoured first are open. Anthium, the Bellone revived from 2012, is among the others. The founder, his wife and his son are never named and listed in people.json, the founder and his wife as precautions.

picks.why: Barile house of 1925, in a village whose cellars are cut into the volcanic tuff, a historic name of traditional, long aged Aglianico del Vulture; Don Anselmo, first made in 1985 and named in the founder's honour, is its classic bottling.
picks.note: Answered: Don Anselmo reads Aglianico del Vulture Superiore DOCG on the house's English page and its later sheets and Aglianico del Vulture DOC on its Italian product page and the earlier listings, so the record gives both and the year the label first read Superiore stays open. The Tommasi family of Valpolicella took a majority in mid August 2016, by Tommasi's own notice, its share kept private. The library's Rotondo is Barone Rotondo from the 2020 vintage. Whether the house still cellars in the tuff of Barile, beside a newer winery of 2006 in one account, is open. The founder (born 1898 by the house) and his son are described, never named; the family's living members are listed in people.json.

picks.why: Barile estate of 2000 at the foot of Monte Vulture, whose old vines in the highest part of Contrada Solagna del Titolo give Titolo, the founding wine and the Aglianico del Vulture the library sets against Taurasi; a Titolo Superiore and a Superiore Riserva from the same vineyard now stand beside it.
picks.note: Answered: Contrada Solagna del Titolo at Barile, at about 600 metres, by the house, Città del Vino and Decanter through K&L. The house carries its living founder's name: the house may be named, the person never in prose, and she is listed in people.json with the grandfather of the 1960s and the great grandfather, both described and never named. Open: the label of a recent vintage (DOC in the page's heading, DOCG Superiore in its field of denomination); Titolo by Amphora is not taught.

picks.why: Rionero in Vulture house of 1998 whose barriques age in tuff caves of the seventeenth century, by its account, and whose wines take notarial names; La Firma, the signature, from Aglianico picked in the first days of November, is the Aglianico del Vulture taught here beside the house's Il Repertorio and Il Sigillo.
picks.note: Answered: 1998 by the house, L'AcquaBuona and Vinoway. La Firma is Aglianico del Vulture DOC on the house's sheet and its 2019 page; Vinous reports Superiore bottlings in 2011 and 2014 and a plan for Superiore from the 2019 vintage, and a merchant's blog a 2021 DOCG, so the label of recent vintages is open. Open as well: whether the notary of the name is the founder's father or grandfather, La Firma's first vintage, and whether settlers of 1533 dug the caves before the friars. The founder and his wife are living, never named, and listed in people.json.

picks.why: Cirò Marina family house, bottling since 1953 on Via Tirone, a reference for Cirò and, from its research of 1993, for the revival of Calabria's native grapes; Duca Sanfelice, Gaglioppo alone from the old bush vines of Ponta aged in steel, is its Cirò Rosso Classico Superiore Riserva, while the house calls Gravello its flagship.
picks.note: Answered: the house writes Duca Sanfelice in one word on its own pages. Gravello, Gaglioppo with Cabernet Sauvignon first made in 1988, is the house's flagship by its own page and is taught in others, a trap and a question. The author put a swap to Gravello under a new key to the checker, and the refuter refused it on 2026-11-14, as reviews/check-calabria-basilicata.json records: the group teaches Calabria, the region record names Cirò as its signature red, and Duca Sanfelice is the house's Cirò of Gaglioppo alone, while Gravello is labelled outside the appellation. The record was not rewritten, so no swap is recorded and the integrator may revisit it if the owner reads flagship as the house's word alone. Open: how Duca Sanfelice is labelled after the Cirò Classico DOCG of 2025, and two years in steel against about three for one vintage. Founded is empty (1950, 1953). The founder, his two sons and the third generation are never named; the living are listed in people.json.

picks.why: Family estate at Contrada Palazzi on the Ionian coast at Casignana, beside Bianco, carried on by the founder's son and grandson by its own account, making the passito Greco di Bianco, a DOC whose rules allow one sweet wine of dried grapes.
picks.note: Answered: the estate is at Contrada Palazzi, Casignana Mare, by its own site, Italian Wine Directory and the Wine Scholar Guild, not Caraffa del Bianco. Founded is empty: the early 1900s on one page of the house and 1958 on another. The bottling taught is the classic Greco di Bianco aged in steel under a light label; the black label, aged in barriques, and the Mantonico passito go in others. The first DOC of the province of Reggio Calabria rests on one source and is cut; the loss of weight in drying is not taught. The founder's son and grandson are described, never named, and listed in people.json.

picks.why: Corullón house of the Palacios family of Rioja and Priorat, established late in the 1990s (1998 by one importer's sheet) and making its first wine in 1999, on steep slate and quartzite terraces; La Faraona is the high single plot at the head of the ladder the house built, and the library holds it as a wine record of its own.
picks.note: Answered: no rank of Bierzo's ladder of 2017 is borne out for La Faraona by the Consejo or a label (merchants' Viña Clasificada and Gran Viña Clasificada set against the Consejo's timetable of 2025 and 2030), so classification stays empty until a label or the Consejo is read. The library also holds the wine as w-la-faraona; wave one's Priorat house of the family is another house and another wine. Founded keeps the library's 1999. The son and the nephew who founded the house are living, never named, and already in people.json; the patriarch of the house's name is described, never named, for want of his dates.

picks.why: Valtuille de Abajo grower who learnt his trade at the family's Castro Ventosa and began his own Ultreia range in 2003, by the house's account, then carried the same ways west into Ribeira Sacra and Rías Baixas; Ultreia Saint Jacques, Mencía from old vines around Valtuille, is the house's wide release.
picks.note: Answered: the house prints Ultreia Saint Jacques on its own page and the importer Ultreia St. Jacques, with Bierzo; the record keeps Saint Jacques. Founded is empty (2003 for the range by the house, 2005 for the company by two accounts), and the site of Villegas is given for one vintage only. The library's consultancy is borne out by one importer and is not in the record. The house is named for a living man, so the prose says the house or the grower, never the name standing for the person; he, his nephew at Castro Ventosa and his partner in Sketch are listed in people.json. The family bodega is Castro Ventosa, a pick of this group, and the two stories are kept apart.

picks.why: Valtuille de Abajo family bodega named for the walled hill above its cellar, its family growing vines in the village since 1752 by its own account; Valtuille Cepas Centenarias, first made with the 1999 vintage, is its Mencía from vines more than a century old, in later vintages from the single plot of Mata los Pardos.
picks.note: Answered: the century old vines are the house's own, at Mata los Pardos by its page, and the vineyards since 1752 are the house's account. No single founding year holds (1752, the first bottling of 1989, the name of the 1990s), so founded is empty; the year the bodega took the hill's name (1991, or the middle of the 1990s) is open. The why's sandy valley floor is not borne out (the house names a plot, not a soil, and one listing gives clay) and is gone. The merge read is answered by the refuter: the bodega and the grower's own range are two houses of one family with two wines, their stories kept apart (the bodega of 1752, 1989 and the 1990s against the range of 2003), each trap telling which is which, so no swap is proposed. The family's living members are never named and listed in people.json.

picks.why: Bierzo Alto bodega of 2000 at San Román de Bembibre, working old Mencía bush vines on slate and clay; Cepas Viejas, its first wine, is its old vine Mencía aged in oak, the riper, oak shaped face of the Bierzo of the early 2000s.
picks.note: Answered: 2000 is borne out by three independent pages, and the slate and clay by the listings. The flagship is the Mencía, Dominio de Tares Cepas Viejas, Bierzo; the barrel fermented Godello of the same name goes in others, and the year it took the name is not settled and is left out. French and American oak in some vintages, French alone on the house's sheet of 2022, so the making says oak. The person interviewed for the house is never named and listed in people.json.

picks.why: Cacabelos house at Pieros on the pilgrims' road, recovering old Mencía on the clay soils of the valley, worked as many small plots; Losada is its namesake Mencía, the way into a range that climbs to Altos de Losada and La Bienquerida.
picks.note: Answered: founded stays empty (2005 in most accounts, 2004 in two); the label is Losada with Bierzo on the house's page; La Bienquerida's Vino de Paraje of Las Chas is borne out by the house's own pages, not by a Consejo page, and its first year is not in the record. One merchant calls Altos de Losada the house's flagship; the namesake Losada is kept as the wine a guest meets first, and the record claims no rank for it. The winemaker and the architect of the cellar are never named and listed in people.json.

picks.why: Rioja house of 1858 at Elciego that came to Rueda around 1970 with its Bordeaux consultant, by the denomination's history, and made its first Rueda whites in 1972, by its own; its cold fermented Rueda Verdejo is the white with which, the region record says, modern Rueda began.

Open: the meaning of the name 7 Fuentes, and the tier word Vino de Villa met on two retailers. Nobody living is named; the son who leads the house and his father are listed in people.json.

picks.why: Group begun in 2005 by four friends who had studied oenology together at the Miguel Hernández University, first as a consultancy, working old own rooted vineyards in Tenerife, the Ribeira Sacra and Almansa; Benje Tinto, mostly Listán Prieto from old bush vines at about 1,000 metres around Santiago del Teide in the west of the island, sold under the DO Ycoden-Daute-Isora, is the house's Canary red to know.
picks.note: Answered: 2005 by Grandi Bottiglie and Cru World Wine; Listán Prieto with Tintilla and some Listán Blanco in some vintages; Santiago del Teide at about 1,000 metres; the DO Ycoden-Daute-Isora by Decanter's review and listings, the order's list of municipalities not read; the record is about Tenerife, with Táganan, Lousas and Almansa named as the group's other places. Open: no primary source of the group's own was found, so the wine rests on the importer's sheets; whether some vintages age partly in concrete. Envínate is not in the region record's producers line, which the integrator may wish to add. The four founders are living, never named, and listed in people.json.

picks.why: The growers' co-operative of Fuencaliente on La Palma, Llanovid, whose wines carry the Teneguía name, at the volcanic southern tip of the island where most of the Malvasía for its sweet wine grows; its Malvasía Aromática Dulce, sweet with the grape's own sugar from overripe, late picked grapes and never fortified, is the heir the region record names to the sweet Canary of history.
picks.note: Answered: Llanovid the co-operative and Teneguía its brand on two accounts; founded is empty, the winery dated 1945 by some and 1947 by others; the label words stay open (Malvasía Aromática Dulce, or naturalmente dulce on a medal of 2024); Estelar is left out on one guide; the record says it is a co-operative. Open: no technical sheet of the co-operative's sweet Malvasía was found, so its vessels and time in tank or wood are unknown; whether the San Antonio volcano erupted in 1677, reported in the review as a plausible tension with the region record. The co-operative's winemaker is living, never named, and listed in people.json.

picks.why: Getaria family house whose records, by its own account, place its vines in the town from 1649, a new generation of which set out in 1980 to revive Getaria's txakoli and is counted among those who pressed for the Getariako Txakolina DO of 1989; its white, mostly Hondarrabi Zuri from slopes above the sea, pale, sharp and faintly prickling, is the plain statement of Getaria's txakoli, poured from a height.
picks.note: Answered: the family's part in the DO of 1989 rests on the house and on two pages that name the leader of the revival among the DO's founders; the records of 1649 are the family's account of the notarial archives of Gipuzkoa, repeated everywhere and never with a reference; the label words are Getariako Txakolina and the house's name. The why's white of Hondarrabi Zuri is set right as mostly Hondarrabi Zuri, since merchants give a share of Beltza. Open: the archive of 1649 itself; the training of the vines, pergola or wires; the share of Hondarrabi Beltza, a twentieth to a half on merchants' sheets against Hondarrabi Zuri alone on the house's. No living member of the family is named; the member said to have led the revival of 1980 is listed in people.json, and the Txueka Etxaniz line is named as a family, as the house names itself.

picks.why: Getaria family house making txakoli there since 1820 by its own account, 1860 by its importer, its vines trained high on the parral above the sea; Rubentis, its still rosé of Hondarrabi Beltza and Hondarrabi Zuri, about half of each, picked and fermented together with native yeasts and bottled with its own natural prickle, is the pink face of Getaria the region record names the house for.
picks.note: Answered: Rubentis is Getariako Txakolina, a rosé of Hondarrabi Beltza and Zuri fermented together; the about half of each rests on the importer and a Spanish guide and was not contradicted; 1820 by the family's account and several pages, 1860 by its importer, so founded stays empty; the classic white is the other wine, with Hijo de Rubentis the sparkling rosé made by the traditional method. Open: five generations or seven; Hijo de Rubentis's time on its lees by vintage; native yeasts by most pages against a selection of the house's own by one. No living member of the family is named; its head is listed in people.json.

picks.why: Bizkaiko Txakolina house set up by a group of growers in 1994 by its own account, its first vineyard planted at Muskiz in 1989 and its first wine dated 1995 at a small winery there, the cellar moving to Gernika in the Urdaibai reserve early in the 2000s; Itsasmendi 7, first made in 2003, Hondarrabi Zuri and Zerratia with a share of Riesling kept months on its lees in steel, is its fuller white, built to age in bottle.
picks.note: Answered in part: the why's Gernika house of 1995 ran two facts together, now set apart: 1994 is the house's own founding, 1995 its first wine at Muskiz, and the move to Gernika 2003 by the house's account, 2001 or 2002 by others, so founded is empty. The grapes of 7 are Hondarrabi Zuri, Zerratia (the Basque name for Petit Courbu) and Riesling in every account; the first crianza txakoli of its DO is hedged as the house's claim. Open: why the wine is called 7, found nowhere; the years of the move and the founding (1989, 1994 or 1995 by different pages); a new winery at Gernika of 2020 on one page, not used. No living person is named; the winemaker met in a newspaper's title is listed in people.json, and the founders are described.

picks.why: Bakio estate on the coast of Bizkaia whose farmhouse was built before 1852, its wine kept for the family's table until the middle of the twentieth century and sold by the 1970s, then taken on by a new team of partners in the middle of the 1990s to revive Bakio's vines; Gorrondona, its white for every day, mostly Hondarrabi Zuri with small shares of Zerratia and Mune Mahatsa and a touch of Hondarrabi Beltza, each plot fermented apart with its own yeasts, is the house's wine to know, and Beltza, its young red of Hondarrabi Beltza alone, the region's rarer face.
picks.note: Answered: Gorrondona is the white's name on its label (DGTX on the house's newer bottles, from 2024 by two pages); its blend is Hondarrabi Zuri with Zerratia, Mune Mahatsa and a touch of Beltza, so the why's a little Hondarrabi Beltza, short of the whole, is set right; Doniene is the lees aged white. The sale of the 1970s is no longer given to the provincial government, whose page could not be told apart in the results. Open: 1994 or 1996 for the team's arrival and the company; whether a trap should name DGTX; the renaming of the red with the 2018 vintage, not tested. No living person is named; the four partners are listed in people.json.

picks.why: Okondo estate in the Ayala valley of Álava, a family project whose first vines were planted in 1996 on the south slope of Mount Ganekogorta, its winery built among them in 2007 by its own account and 2008 by others; Astobiza, its white of Hondarrabi Zuri kept months on its fine lees and then in bottle, is the way into Arabako Txakolina, the youngest of the three txakoli DOs, recognised in 2001.
picks.note: Answered: the winery and the first harvest are 2007 by MiVino and the house, 2008 by Field Blend Selections and Bodeboca, so founded stays empty as the plan allowed and the why's first harvest of 2007 is now the house's winery of 2007; the label is Astobiza, sold as Señorío de Astobiza by merchants. Izkiriota, the Basque name for Gros Manseng, is the late harvest wine's grape, not the white's, which is Hondarrabi Zuri alone on the house's shop sheet and with about a tenth of Zerratia on its older pages; Malkoa, aged in concrete eggs, is its white for laying down. Open: 250 or 300 metres; the months on the lees by vintage. No living person is named; the founder of the family project is described.

picks.why: O Bolo house of 2004 in the Bibei valley of Valdeorras, set up by a younger member of the Palacios family who bought old Godello vineyards from elderly local growers; As Sortes is Godello alone from six small sortes planted in the late 1970s and early 1980s at Santa Cruz do Bolo, above 680 metres on sandy, decomposed granite, fermented and aged about eight months in 500 litre oak barrels on its lees, by the house's own page.
picks.note: Answered: the label is As Sortes, Val do Bibei, Valdeorras, and the six sortes, their planting by local growers, Santa Cruz do Bolo and the height above 680 metres are on the house's own page. The large wood the why once gave is true of the first vintages (the 2005 in 3,000 litre foudres by one vertical) and of Louro, made in 35 hectolitre foudres, while As Sortes is made in 500 litre barrels; the library's style line is reported in the review and not edited. The ReViVal of 1974 and Godello's near loss are the DO's own account. Open: the vintage the making changed, Louro's little Treixadura (the library's alone) and the ReViVal's first year (1974 by the Xunta and the DO's fiftieth year, 1975 on one DO page). The house keeps its name and the man is never named in prose, said as a younger member of the Palacios family; he is listed in people.json, so another record names the house by its place, as Dominio do Bibei's trap now does.

picks.why: Valdeorras family estate at Rubiá in the Sil valley, replanted with Godello alone from 1985 by the brothers of the Guitián family when the grape was all but forgotten, the wines taking the family's name; Guitián Godello Sobre Lías is made in stainless steel and kept four to six months on its fine lees, stirred weekly, with no oak, the barrel fermented Godello of the middle 1990s beside it in others.
picks.note: Answered: the house is Bodegas A Tapada at Rubiá, founded in 1985 with the brothers' replanting, by the house's own pages and three accounts; the label taught is Guitián Godello Sobre Lías, chosen over the barrel wine, which stands in others with its first told as the house's claim. Godeval, the alternative, was not needed and no swap was proposed. Open: the first barrel fermented Godello (1996 by the house, 1995 or trials of 1994 by others), the first Guitián of 1992 and the building of the winery, none of them told. The brother who led the project and died in a road accident about ten years after the founding is described, his dates found nowhere; the brother and sister who carried the house on and its two consulting oenologists are never named and are listed in people.json.

picks.why: Doade house of the Amandi subzone of Ribeira Sacra, whose family took on a run of half ruined terraces above the Sil in 1979 and began to rebuild them; Pizarra, Spanish for slate, is its Mencía, alone or very nearly so, from south facing slate terraces, aged twelve to eighteen months by vintage in French oak barrels and foudres.
picks.note: Answered: founded stays empty, since 1979, 1980, 1996, 1998 and 2005 are all given; Pizarra is Mencía alone or very nearly so by the house's sheet and the merchants', and no page calls it the flagship, so the thin region rule lets the pick stand as the house's barrel aged Mencía and its most listed red. The founding winery of the DO of 1996 the why once gave rests on one producer guide and is dropped: the DO was first recognised in 1995 and confirmed with its rules by the order of 3 September 1996. The native grape reds are Risco (Merenzao) and Serradelo (Brancellao), in others with Carravel, a Mencía of chosen plots. Open: the vineyard's spelling (Carballo Cobo or Carballocovo), Pizarra's own vineyard, and the fifteen centuries of vines, told as the house's. The founder, his wife and their son are never named; the founder and his wife are listed in people.json.

picks.why: Estate of the Bibei valley at Manzaneda in Quiroga-Bibei, Ribeira Sacra's eastern subzone by the Valdeorras border, founded in the early 2000s by a businessman returning to his family's roots, its first wines of the 2002 vintage; Lalama is its red of Mencía with small shares of Brancellao, Mouratón, Sousón and a Garnacha, fermented with native yeasts in large open wooden vats and raised in used barrels and foudres for a year and more.
picks.note: Answered: the label is Lalama, Ribeira Sacra; the Garnacha is given as the sheets give it (Garnacha, Garnacha Tintorera or Alicante Bouschet); founded stays empty for 2000, 2001 or 2002; Lacima is the house's other red by the Consejo's directory and Galicia en Vinos. The house's whites are Lapena and Lapola both, Godello based, so the earlier note's Lapena was right and the author's correction of it was not; Lalume is a Ribeiro white led by Treixadura. Open: which Garnacha, the heights (from about 300 metres to 700 and higher by different sheets) and the two whites' blends. The founder, his brother and the Priorat consultants said to have helped from 2002 are never named and are listed in people.json.

picks.why: The trading name of Vitivinícola del Ribeiro, the growers' co-operative at Valdepereira, Ribadavia, founded in 1968; Viña Costeira is its everyday white, a blend led by Treixadura with Torrontés, Godello, Albariño and Loureira in shares that change by year, each variety fermented apart at low temperature in steel and the blend bottled young without oak.
picks.note: Answered: the co-operative is Vitivinícola del Ribeiro, founded in 1968 by Campo Galego and three accounts, and the record says it is a co-operative. That Colección 68 is named for the year rests on one account and stays out, so the earlier note's claim is withdrawn; Colección 68 is a blend led by Treixadura with Albariño and Godello, not Treixadura alone. The ordinances of 1579, the protection of 1932 and the council of 6 December 1956 are the DO's own account. Open: 1579 or 1594 for the ordinances, Pazo as the first bottled Ribeiro, and the return to the native grapes, dated to the 1990s by one source and left undated in the record. No living person is named or met.

picks.why: The Melgaço family estate whose first vineyard of Alvarinho, by its own account the first continuous vineyard of the grape in the municipality, was planted in 1974, and whose first wine, bottled in the family garage in 1982, became by its own account the first Alvarinho brand of Melgaço; Soalheiro Alvarinho is fermented cool in steel and kept on its fine lees, with no oak.
picks.note: Answered: the vineyard of 1974 and the brand of 1982 are the house's own account, borne out by Decanter's vertical and an importer beside it, and the first brand is hedged as the house's claim; the founder worked in the local finance office. Primeiras Vinhas and Granit, from plots at about 400 metres, are in others. The carried the grape abroad the why once gave was never tested and is dropped, as is the region record's most widely poured name abroad, a ranking. The library's no added spritz rests on no source read either way, so the record makes no claim on carbon dioxide, reported in the review. Open: the garage of 1982 and the wife's teaching, told as the house's. The founder and the next generation are never named; the founder and the oenologist of the next generation are listed in people.json.

picks.why: The neoclassical palace and walled estate at Pinheiros, just south of Monção, built from about the turn of the nineteenth century to about 1834, classed a national monument by the decree of 16 June 1910 and bought in 1937 as a gift for a daughter, Maria Hermínia d'Oliveira Paes (1918 to 2015); by the house's account she began planting its Alvarinho in 1964, had the cellar built in 1974 and launched the estate Alvarinho in 1976.
picks.note: Answered: 1976, the cellar of 1974 and the Alvarinho of 1964 are the house's and Executiva's; the building and the decree of 1910 are the DGLAB's; the purchase of 1937 is in four accounts; the woman is named with her dates, given by three sources. The why's made the grape's name before most growers bottled it found no source in the author's reading or the refuter's and is dropped, as is the region record's before anyone else bottled it, reported in the review. Open: whether she or her companion planted the vines, built the cellar and launched the wine (the house and Executiva credit her, other accounts her companion after an auction), told as the house's account with the tension named; 1976 or 1977 for the first release; the sale of 2025, left out as recent and on one source. Her companion, whose dates were not found, and the agronomist consulted in 1964 are described or left out and are listed in people.json as precautions; the builder of the palace and his son are described for want of dates.

picks.why: The Melgaço house founded in 1998 by an oenologist born in Monção, whose first Alvarinhos were made at Quinta dos Muros in Penso and which became known for testing what Alvarinho can take, from long lees ageing to skin contact in Curtimenta and new oak in Parcela Única; Muros Antigos is its unoaked Alvarinho, settled cold, fermented cool in steel and stirred on its fine lees for at least three months.
picks.note: Answered: the founder is described, never named, and the house keeps his name; Muros Antigos's making is on the house's sheet and two merchants'; Curtimenta and Parcela Única are in others, Parcela Única's new 400 litre barrels and nine months on three merchants. The sub-region is told rightly: the order of 16 January 2001 drew a sub-region named Monção that took in Melgaço, and the order of 23 March 2009 renamed it Monção e Melgaço. The library's old wood for the house's holdings fits no wine read and the region record's word for the house's bottlings is a judgement; both are reported in the review and neither is repeated. Open: Quinta dos Muros by that name (the house's page alone), 1997 or 1998 for the start, and three or four months on the lees by vintage. The founder is listed in people.json, his name allowed on this record alone.

picks.why: The Penafiel house of the Guedes family, which dates its company to 1870, when a forebear built a cellar at Quinta da Aveleda for 300 barrels; Casal Garcia, launched in 1939 after a French winemaker's visit and named for the vineyard its grapes came from, is a blend of Trajadura, Loureiro, Arinto and Fernão Pires by the house's recent sheet, medium dry, low in alcohol and lightly prickling, not a sparkling wine.
picks.note: Answered: 1939 is on the house's timeline and in Jornal de Negócios; the blend on the house's sheet is Trajadura, Loureiro, Arinto and Fernão Pires, with Azal in older accounts and on several retailers', and the record says so. The why's lightly sparkling is set right, since the record teaches the light prickle as part of the style and not a sparkling wine, and its carried the region's name abroad is dropped, a claim no source read bore out. Open: Azal or Fernão Pires, the vintage of the change unknown, and the year of the French winemaker's visit (1936 or 1937 by the house, 1938 or 1939 by the press), told as the late 1930s. The founder of 1870, the third generation and the French winemaker are described for want of dates; the fourth and fifth generations who have led the company are never named and are listed in people.json.

picks.why: The estate on the Lima at Refóios do Lima, by Ponte de Lima, with records from 1710, which passed to a family in the 1990s and by its own account became a pioneer of Loureiro bottled as a single grape; Esporão bought it in 2019. Ameal Loureiro is pressed whole, fermented in steel at 16 to 18 degrees Celsius and kept about seven months on its fine lees.
picks.note: Answered: the label is Ameal on Esporão's sheets and Quinta do Ameal on older bottles; the history before 2019 is the 1990s in the record, the father's purchase of 1990 and a first Loureiro of 1999 each on one source; the Reserva of the Marinhas plot, once Escolha and begun with trials in French oak in 2000, is in others. The why's could age is now the house's own word of good evolution over a few years, the Reserva its wine for longer keeping. Open: the distance of about 30 kilometres from the Atlantic, on Esporão's page as the author read it. The father and the son of the 1990s are never named; the son is listed in people.json.

picks.why: A family estate at Abrunhosa do Mato between Mangualde and Nelas, one of the estates that grew, made and bottled their own wine in the Dão's revival after the co-operative years; by the house's own account it began bottling reds of a single grape with the 1996 vintage, made only in years it judges good enough, Touriga Nacional among them, and added an Encruzado made alone in 1998, about half of it fermented in barrel.
picks.note: Answered: the varietal Touriga Nacional from the 1996 vintage is on the house's own page, with the Encruzado of 1998; no first is claimed, since Sogrape claims the Dão's first Encruzado at Carvalhais in 1992.
