The why's barrel fermented Encruzado is set right: the house's sheets give about half in French oak barrels, the rest in steel. The making is the house's sheet: wholly destemmed, fermented in steel, fourteen to seventeen months by vintage in 225 litre French oak. Open: the altitude of about 450 metres (merchants and a writer, never the house) and the year of Quinta das Maias. The family is never named; the elder of the family, the son in law who makes the wines and the founder of the importer whose name a source title once carried are listed in people.json.

picks.why: The estate at Pinhanços near Seia, under the Serra da Estrela, whose records of the sixteenth century show it paying its tax in barrels of wine, inherited in 1980 by a civil engineer of the family who set out to make wine there again, its sister Quinta de Saes carrying the first label with the 1989 vintage; Carrocel is Touriga Nacional alone from one small parcel of old vines, made only in good years, fermented in steel and aged eighteen months to two years and more in used French oak barrels of 400 to 500 litres.
picks.note: Answered: the label is Quinta da Pellada Carrocel, Touriga Nacional alone, the library's old vine flagship and a parcel of old vines on three sheets; Primus, a white field blend led by Encruzado and Bical, and Quinta de Saes are in others. Pape is left out: the earlier note's Pape without its living partner was loose, since Pape is a red of Pellada alone and Doda, once Dado, is the collaboration with the Douro house. The library's record of the house gives the country as Spain and Portugal and calls Pape a collaboration; both are reported in the review and not edited. Open: Vila Nova de Tazém or Pinhanços for the estate's parish, Carrocel's planting year and age, and the record of 1527, tied to Saes by one guide. The winemaker, his daughter, the two who have worked with the estates since 2005 and the partners of Doda are never named and are listed in people.json, the library's own producer name in both its printed forms.

picks.why: Sogrape's estate near Mangualde, bought and planted in 1988 with the Dão's own grapes, the company having worked in the region since 1957 by its own history; its Encruzado is begun in steel and moved partway through fermentation into new French oak barrels, the rest kept in steel, then stirred on its fine lees for six to eight months, with Único, the red made only in some years, beside it.
picks.note: Answered: the making rests on the house's sheets as an importer and merchants host them, of 2016, 2021 and 2023; 1957 and 1988 are Sogrape's own dates with no second account read; Único and Parcela 45, the Alfrocheiro whose vineyard the fire of October 2017 burnt, are in others. The why's reference for Encruzado is a ranking and is dropped. Open: Sogrape's first Encruzado of the Dão in 1992 against Roques's varietal Encruzado of 1998, neither told, and six or eight months on the lees. The estate's winemakers and the family who lead Sogrape are never named; the winemaker since 2014 and the chairman are listed in people.json as precautions, from the reader's knowledge rather than a source.

picks.why: The wine house of the old manor estate of Santar near Nelas, founded by its own account at the end of the eighteenth century, which has kept a library of its own old wines since 1955; its Reserva is a blend of about half Touriga Nacional with Alfrocheiro and Aragonez, the Tinta Roriz of the north, wholly destemmed, fermented with a long maceration and part aged in French oak.
picks.note: Answered: founded stays empty (the end of the eighteenth century by the house, 1790 and 1765 in two guides); the Reserva's grapes are on the house's sheet in words; Reserva is the national traditional mention. The why's among the first houses to bottle estate Dão is borne out in neither the author's searches nor the refuter's and is dropped; the region record's line is reported in the review, unconfirmed rather than refuted. The Condessa de Santar white was not found, so the Vinha dos Amores Encruzado stands in others. Open: whether the Dão's own rules add an ageing to Reserva, the barriques and the private winery of the co-operative years (one source each), and a partnership of 2006 not borne out. The countess, the house's winemaker and the winemaker of the 2006 news are never named; the house's winemaker is listed in people.json.

picks.why: An estate born in 1892, as the house tells it, at Passarella in Lagarinhos near Gouveia on the slopes of the Serra da Estrela, whose Villa Oliveira was first bottled in 1893; bought by new owners in 2007 or 2008 and restored, it brought Villa Oliveira back with the 2009 vintage, its Touriga Nacional picked alone from one old field blend vineyard of more than eighty years, fermented with its own yeasts in concrete and aged one to two years in 225 litre French oak.
picks.note: Answered: the house of 1892 stands on the house and two independent accounts, and the first bottling of 1893 and the return of 2009 on three; the vineyard of more than eighty years is on two sheets, about eighty at the 2009 harvest on another; the refugee of the Second World War is told as the house tells it; the Villa Oliveira Encruzado and the Vinha Centenária are in others. Open: 2007 or 2008 for the sale, both told; the founder, named two ways in two accounts with no dates and so not named; the refugee's trade, a winemaker only in the house's telling. Those who revived the estate and its winemaker are never named and are listed in people.json.

picks.why: The house near Anadia whose founder's father began to bottle his own wine in 1970, among the first growers of the Bairrada to do so, and whose founder made his first wine, a red of Baga alone, in 1980 and argued for Baga as a fine grape; the single vineyard reds came in 1995, and Vinha Barrosa is Baga alone from a vineyard on chalky clay planted, by the house's account, in 1900, labelled a regional wine from the 1999 vintage in protest, with the ungrafted Pé Franco on sand beside it.
picks.note: Answered: Vinha Barrosa's soil is chalky clay on an importer's estate notes and a merchant's account, the reddish clay heavier than the family's other plots cut; the label is Vinho Regional from the 1999 vintage, a protest at an appointment by the founder's account, Beiras on the early labels; the making is tied to its vintages, about a year in Allier casks in the 2010s and two years in Portuguese and French oak for the 2021. The why's single vineyard wines from the 1980s are set right as the reds of 1995, and its old bush vines, found in no source read, are dropped. The Pé Franco and Vinha Pan are in others. Open: Monopólio from the 2008 or the 2009 vintage, told as the late 2000s; whether the house returned to DOC Bairrada in 2008 while Vinha Barrosa kept a regional label; Beiras or Beira Atlântico on recent labels; the year the last part of the vineyard was bought. The founder, his father and his daughter are never named and are listed in people.json, the founder's name allowed on this record alone as the house's; the library's record of the house gives its country as Spain and Portugal and calls the Pé Franco a judgement word, both reported in the review and not edited.

picks.why: The family house at São João da Azenha near Anadia, founded in 1920 by three brothers of the Costa family to trade at first in Douro wines and liqueurs, which turned to its own region, launched its Frei João brand towards the end of the 1950s and kept back wine of the vintages it judged strongest, so that Frei João Reserva has been released from vintages as old as the 1960s; the old cellar Reservas are Baga alone, the recent ones mostly Baga with Touriga Nacional.
picks.note: Answered: Frei João Reserva Tinto is taught; the making is the house's sheet of the 2014 and of the 2019, about six months in French oak casks and about eighteen more in cement vats; Porta dos Cavaleiros, the house's Dão of the end of the 1950s, Frei João Tinto and Quinta do Poço do Lobo are in others. The why's kept for years before release is set right as wine held back for decades. Open: Poço do Lobo bought in 1971 or 1972, told as the early 1970s; a Reserva listed with Syrah and Cabernet Sauvignon and casks of 450 litres, on one listing each and neither taught; the Port law of the 1930s as the turn to the Bairrada and to sparkling wine, on one account and left out. The three brothers are described, never named, their dates found in no source; they and the French winemaker one account ties to the turn to sparkling wine are long dead in all likelihood, left out of the prose and not listed in people.json.

picks.why: The family estate at Fogueira, in the parish of Sangalhos near Anadia, which began in 1989 to bottle and sell wine under its own name from vineyards handed down from the founder's grandfathers, whose grapes had long been sold in bulk, and which keeps to the old ways: Baga with its stems in open lagares, aged in large old wooden tonéis and bottled without fining or filtering; its Garrafeira red, from vines of more than ninety years, is made only in the years the family judges exceptional, and its sparkling wines are riddled by hand on wooden pupitres.
picks.note: Answered: the Garrafeira's label and making are on the house's own wines page and its sheet (not destemmed, five to eight days in open lagares punched down by hand, about eighteen months in tonéis, unfined and unfiltered); the native yeast is cut, the house stating it only for its whites; the Reserva is Baga with Touriga Nacional, not Baga alone, and with the Bruto Natural it is in others. The why's long lees ageing for the sparkling wines was never tested and is dropped, as is its classic Bairrada to know. Open: the vines' age, more than ninety years by the house and well over a century by one merchant; the Rota da Bairrada's first new wine company in more than twenty years, told as its account on one source. The founder is never named and is listed in people.json in two printed forms; his grandfathers are described, one known by a lone forename and long dead in all likelihood, and are not listed.

picks.why: A family estate at Sangalhos near Anadia that by its own account has made wine for more than half a century across three generations; its Garrafeira red, from Baga vines of about eighty years on sandy clay and made only in years the house judges exceptional, is fermented in small open lagares with the cap of skins pushed down into the must again and again, then given about two years in oak and a further year in bottle before release, for long ageing.
picks.note: Answered: the Garrafeira's making is on the house's own page; Baga alone is cut, the house giving old vine Baga without alone and a merchant the 2016 as made primarily of Baga; the why's trodden in lagar and old wood are set right as the house's skins pushed down and its two years in oak; founded stays empty, the house giving only more than half a century and three generations, and the start of its own bottling 1992 or the late 1980s by two accounts. The white Garrafeira and the Pinot Noir of 2017 are in others, and a trap now says the Reserva is the blend of Baga and Touriga Nacional. Open: foot treading in stone lagares (merchants) beside the house's own words, and clay limestone (one merchant) against the house's sandy clay. The woman who ran the estate, dead early in 2022 by one account and undated, her son and her son in law are never named and are listed in people.json, she as a precaution.

picks.why: The hotel in the palace of the Buçaco forest, where the Bairrada meets the Dão, whose wines began by most accounts in 1917 and took in 1920 the red and white labels they have carried with little change since: Baga of the Bairrada with Touriga Nacional of the Dão, a blend neither DOC allows, so they are sold as table wine; for most of their history the hotel blended and aged bought wines in its own cellar, and from about 2000 it has made the wine from bought grapes at Curia, the red then given about a year in French oak.
picks.note: Answered in part: Buçaco Reservado Tinto and Vinho de Mesa are on Decanter's listing of the 2011, the category since renamed Vinho; the old cellar vintages are borne out by the accounts read. The why's aged for years before release is set right as about a year in 300 litre French oak by two merchants, the years in bottle resting on the importer alone; made in its own cellar since 1917 is set right as bought finished wine for most of its history. Open: the start in 1917 (most accounts) or a first bottling in the 1920s (one); the labels of 1920, on the author's importer and a merchant only; Reservado as a way round the rule on Reserva, of which only the plain meaning is taught; Vinha da Mata's share of Baga; the hotel's opening in 1909, 1911 or 1917, told as by 1917. The concession put to tender in 2024 is not in the record, which names no operator, and the integrator may look again if the cellar closes. The architect, the minister and the king are described, long dead; the hotelier of 1917 and the chef of 1911 are left out, long dead, and none of them is listed in people.json.

picks.why: The co-operative of Colares founded in 1931, by its own account Portugal's oldest wine co-operative, which from the 1930s until a decree of 15 September 1994 held by law the sole right to make Colares, so that for some six decades every bottle of the appellation began in its cellar; Arenae is its Colares of Ramisco from ungrafted vines in the dune sand, fermented in steel and aged about five years, first in large vats of exotic wood and then in smaller oak casks, before it is bottled in half litre bottles.
picks.note: Answered: 1931 is on four pages besides the Adega's own; the claim of the oldest wine co-operative is kept as the Adega's, two pages repeating it; the sole right came by Decreto-Lei 24 500 of 1934 on the preamble of Decreto-Lei 235/94 (1938 in other accounts, so the record says the 1930s) and ended with Decreto-Lei 235/94; Arenae is DOC Colares Ramisco on the Adega's shop and the merchants, its two vessels in that order in the vintages of 2012 to 2020; Arenae Malvasia is in others. The why's old vats is set right as vats of exotic wood and then oak casks. The rules of 12 March 2021 admit the chão rijo as a soil of the appellation and up to a fifth of a Colares from it, so the record no longer says Colares is the sand alone. Open: the year of the law, and the order of the vessels before 2012. Two questions of the Codex and the region record's labels line teach the sand rule and a monopoly from 1931; they are reported in the review and not edited.

picks.why: A Colares house of Almoçageme dating from 1808 by its own account, whose name means the widow Gomes; since the decree of 1994 ended the co-operative's sole right it has made its own Colares again, Ramisco from ungrafted vines in the sand, trodden by foot as whole bunches and aged five years and more in casks of oak, chestnut and Brazilian mahogany, its label keeping the old spelling Collares, and the bottles of the 1960s it has released show how Ramisco from the sand ages over decades.
picks.note: Answered: 1808 is kept as the house's, with Sábado and the parish of Colares; Collares is on the red on Decanter and Vivino, Ramisco on Tourinto's sheets; the tank and the foot treading stand on two accounts, the chestnut is Portuguese on Tourinto's sheets, and the wine's own yeasts, on one importer, are cut. The Malvasia white and the Viticultores wines, from vines inside the Colares area but off the sand, are in others. Open: the years in cask by vintage, kept as five years and more; the year the family that keeps the house bought it, 1988 or the early 1990s, not in the record. The father and the son of that family are never named and are listed in people.json; the founder of 1808, long dead, is left out.

picks.why: The Bucelas estate north of Lisbon, its documents traced by its owners to 1218 and its morgado to 1703, whose Prova Régia, Arinto alone fermented cool in steel and rested on its fine lees with no oak, became the label by which British merchants knew it; its name, royal approval, recalls the story of the Bucelas wine the Duke of Wellington (1769 to 1852) took home in the Peninsular War, and its label reads DOC Bucelas in some vintages and Vinho Regional Lisboa in others; Sogrape's purchase was made public at the start of 2019.
picks.note: Answered: Wine Ventures made the 2017 at the estate; Sogrape's purchase was made public on 4 January 2019, 2018 in other accounts; Romeyra is the old spelling Sogrape took back for the brand; Morgado de Santa Catherina and Prova Régia Reserva are in others; the label is Vinho Regional Lisboa on listings of 2015, 2019 and 2020 and DOC Bucelas on those of 2023 and 2024, and the record says both. The why's made Arinto known abroad is not in the record and is dropped. Open: the label itself, never read; whether vintages before 2019 drew Arinto from across Lisboa (the importer alone); whether Prova Régia carries on under the Quinta da Romeyra identity of 2026; the king, George III or the Prince Regent; royal approval as the importer's gloss, a royal tasting in plain Portuguese. The record tells the history and names no range of 2026, so the pick stands. Sogrape's chief executive quoted on the purchase is never named and is listed in people.json; the sellers are told by no name.

picks.why: The Carcavelos of the Oeiras municipal council, grown on the old estate of the Marquis of Pombal (1699 to 1782) at Oeiras, where the national agronomy station replanted vines in the 1980s and the council later joined it to save the fortified wine of the coast west of Lisbon, which the city's growth had almost erased; its cellar at Casal da Manteiga has been in use since 2001, and Superior 15 Anos is Arinto, Galego Dourado and Ratinho, fortified midway and aged fifteen years on average in Portuguese and French oak.
picks.note: Answered: the replanting is the 1980s (1983 by the council and a book of 1990, 1984 by a paper of 2005, 1985 by Grandes Escolhas); the council's cellar at Casal da Manteiga, an old building in use from 2001, and its sole charge of the station's vineyards after 2006; 7 Anos and Superior 15 Anos on the house's pages and the merchants, one wine under the two words; the Marquis is named with his dates. The why's almost the only maker stays out of the record, Quinta dos Pesos being met on a merchant, and is dropped. Open: the palace cellar recovered in 2012 and the nineteenth century's dry fermentation with vinho abafado, the house's alone and hedged so; Superior as more than ten years in wood on the house's page, where one merchant gives ten years on average. The station's director of 1983 is never named and is listed in people.json as a precaution.

picks.why: The estate near Alenquer, in the hills north of Lisbon, bought by most accounts in 1990 by a gastronome with a passion for the Rhône, who planted it mostly with Syrah from Rhône cuttings and with Viognier; its opening wine came with the 1997 vintage, and its Reserva, Syrah fermented with a few per cent of Viognier as Côte-Rôtie does and aged in French oak, set out to show what Syrah can do in the Atlantic hills of Lisboa; the conversion to organic farming began with the 2006 harvest.
picks.note: Answered: the purchase is 1990 in two accounts and 1986 and 1987 in one each, so founded stays empty and the story says by most accounts in 1990; the Rhône cuttings stand on two accounts; the Reserva is labelled Vinho Regional Lisboa, not DOC Alenquer; the plain red (Syrah with Tinta Roriz and Touriga Nacional in some vintages, Syrah alone being unsure), Madrigal and Parcela 24 are in others. The why's proved Syrah belongs is softened to an aim. Open: the plain red's grapes by vintage, and the Reserva's sixteen to twenty months in oak, not read again. The founder is described as a gastronome, never named, and is listed in people.json.

picks.why: The estate at Almeirim on the Tejo's left bank, born in 1723 by its own account as the Quinta de Vale de Nabais and renamed, as the house tells it, after its founder, Pedro Miguel de Almeida Portugal (1688 to 1756), took the Indian fortress of Alorna in 1746 and was made Marquis of Alorna in 1748; the Marquesa de Alorna range carries the title of his granddaughter, the poet Alcipe, and its Grande Reserva red, a blend the house keeps secret, is aged fourteen months in new French oak and rested at least a year in bottle.
picks.note: Answered: 1723, the fortress taken in 1746 and the marquisate of 1748 are borne out, the renaming hedged as the house's and one magazine's; the red is taught, its grapes the house's secret, and the white and the 1723, a Grande Reserva red of the three hundredth year, are in others; the auction is no longer given to the heirs of the last Countess of Junqueira, who died in 1913 without heirs by one account; 1918 stands on the state heritage inventory and Portugal by Wine. The why's one of the Tejo's oldest names was never tested and is dropped. Open: the buyers from the poet's daughters (the Counts of Junqueira by the house, a viscount of the first half of the nineteenth century by one account); the red's grapes, one listing giving five varieties for the 2016; its fermentation, found nowhere. The family of 1918 is described, never named; the winemaker on a merchant's listing and the author and the writer of the preface of the book of the tricentenary are listed in people.json.

picks.why: A family estate at Almeirim on the Tejo's left bank, held by one family since 1775 by its own account, on land the house says was a royal hunting ground where Portugal's kings flew their falcons; its Falcoaria range, named in homage to those hunts, gathers an oak aged red and whites of old vine Fernão Pires and a late harvest, and Falcoaria Tinto joins Castelão with Alicante Bouschet, Touriga Nacional and Cabernet Sauvignon, fermented in cement and aged about a year in French oak.
picks.note: Answered, with a correction to the why: the house's page and Grandes Escolhas say the range is named for the royal falcon hunts once held on the land, not for the house's own falconry; Falcoaria Tinto is taught, twelve months in French oak on two listings of the 2021 sheet and thirteen on the CVR Tejo's; the DOC do Tejo took the place of DOC Ribatejo by Portaria 140/2010, the Ribatejo's statutes having been approved by Decreto-Lei 45/2000. The why's oak aged whites and reds of traditional grapes are set right as the Fernão Pires and the late harvest the range holds and a red that joins Castelão with Touriga Nacional and Cabernet Sauvignon. Open: the dovecote's age, sixteenth century by the house and nineteenth by one article, out of the record; 1775 by the house and most accounts, 1755 by one; foot treading in cement lagares for part of the oldest vines, one sheet. The family is never named; the member who runs the estate and two of its winemakers are listed in people.json.

picks.why: The Herdade de Muge on the Tejo's left bank, which passed to the house of the Dukes of Cadaval in the seventeenth century when a daughter of the Counts of Odemira married into it, the dukedom created in 1648, the year the house dates its stud of Lusitano horses to; its flagship red bears the title of Olga Nicolis di Robilant (1900 to 1996), the Marquesa de Cadaval, and is Touriga Nacional, Trincadeira and Alicante Bouschet from old vines, given sixteen months in new French oak and a year in bottle.
picks.note: Answered: 1648 is the dukedom and the stud, not a founding, so founded stays empty; the palace held by a queen until 1530 is the house's account, Público naming her; the marquise is named with her dates, in three sources; that the red was named for her was not found, so the record says only that it bears her title; de and do Cadaval both appear; the red's grapes and making are the house's sheet, its fifty year old vines hedged as the sheet for the 2015; the Reserva, the white and the Trincadeira are in others. Open: whether the queen lived at Muge or only held it; whether the red was named for the marquise herself; vines of fifty years against twenty on one merchant. The head of the house since 1998 is never named and is listed in people.json; the Marquis of the marriage of 1926 is described, long dead.

picks.why: The estate beside Alpiarça on the Tejo's left bank, across the river from Santarém, bought in 1834 by the family of the Counts of Póvoa and passed between 1841 and 1842 to its heiress, who married the future second Duke of Palmela, so that it came down through the house of Palmela; its Grande Escolha reds, made only in strong years, were bottled by grape as Syrah and as Alfrocheiro, and the Alfrocheiro taught here is aged ten to twelve months in French oak, new or a year old, its later bottlings named Grande Reserva.
picks.note: Answered: the Grande Escolha Alfrocheiro is taught, the label of the bottles to the 2016, in fifteen editions by Grandes Escolhas, which calls it the estate's flagship; the later Grande Reserva name is taught in the label and the story; the marriage year is left out, 1836 by two genealogies and 1846 by the house, the transfer of 1841 to 1842 standing. The Grande Escolha Syrah, the Reserva of Alfrocheiro and Syrah and Dona Isabel Juliana, a name for Grande Reserva red and white wines and the sparkling wine at the head of the range, are in others. The why's large estate, Touriga Nacional, horses and cork rest on one listing each or on none, are not in the prose and are dropped. No swap: the author's renaming to Grande Reserva Alfrocheiro is refused by the refuter, and the Dona Isabel Juliana Grande Reserva red, first made in 2009 by trade press, was weighed and not taken, since no record has been written or refuted for it. Open: the marriage year; a lagar with mechanical treading for the 2016 and a vineyard of the early 1970s, on one magazine each.

picks.why: The farm company of the lower Tejo's flood meadows and of the Charneca heaths beyond them, formed in June 1836 when the Crown sold the lands to a group of investors, nationalised in 1975 and made by a decree law of 1989 a company of wholly public capital; its first vineyard was planted in 1881 on the Charneca sand at Catapereiro, where its winery stands, and its 1836 Grande Reserva red, named for the year of the founding, is Alicante Bouschet alone, fermented in a lagar with its own yeasts and aged thirteen to eighteen months in French oak by vintage.
picks.note: Answered: the 1836 range is made red, white and sparkling, and the red, Alicante Bouschet alone by the company's sheet, is taught; its oak differs by vintage (thirteen months in new oak for the 2020, fourteen in new oak for the 2012, eighteen half new for the 2016); the nationalisation is 13 November 1975 by an independent account; the place rests on the company's own address, south of the Sorraia; the white, the Bruto and Tyto Alba are in others. The why's yields held down was never tested and is dropped. Open: the month of June 1836, on the company's history page and the author's reading alone; whether Catapereiro lies inside the Tagus Estuary nature reserve, on one account and left out, so the earlier note's vines in the reserve are not carried.

picks.why: The house at Vila Nogueira de Azeitão that keeps the name of its founder, a mathematician from the Dão born in 1804, who set it up in 1834 by the house's account; by its own timeline he created its Moscatel de Setúbal brand in 1849, and its red of the Cova da Periquita was being made by 1850. Alambre, the vintage dated Moscatel de Setúbal of Muscat of Alexandria, fortified, left three to five months on its skins by vintage and aged in used wood, is its plain statement of the style, and the Torna Viagem, the wine of the return voyage, the old custom it revived aboard the Sagres in 2000.
picks.note: Answered: the vintage dated Alambre is taught and the 20 Anos is in others; 1834 is hedged as the house's account and 1849 rests on its timeline alone; the voyage of 2000 aboard the Sagres is borne out by the trade press and the CVR's news; Periquita, made by 1850, and Lancers of 1944 are in others; the Superior of 1911 and the Moscatel Roxo Superior of 1918 are told as released from its old casks. Not the Port house of the same name. Open: the founder's death, 1884 on the house's timeline and 1887 in another account, so he is described and never named with dates; the Paris medal one account ties to 1849 and another to 1855, left out. The house's winemaker, met in the refuter's results, is never named and is listed in people.json.

picks.why: The Azeitão company that began in 1922 as João Pires & Filhos, traded as J.P. Vinhos and later took the name of the Renaissance palace of Bacalhôa, beside which, in 1974, the head of João Pires planted Cabernet Sauvignon and Merlot at the request of the grandson of the palace's American buyer of the 1930s. Quinta da Bacalhôa, first made in 1979 and by the company's account the first Cabernet Sauvignon and Merlot made in Portugal, is Cabernet Sauvignon in the great majority with Merlot, a Vinho Regional Península de Setúbal aged about a year to two in new French oak by vintage.
picks.note: Answered: the planting of 1974 and the first vintage of 1979 are borne out, 1972 in two accounts and left open; the claim of the first Cabernet Sauvignon and Merlot made in Portugal is told as the company's own; the new owners of 1998 are living and never named; Palácio da Bacalhôa, from around the turn of the millennium, the white of the quinta and the ten year Moscatel de Setúbal Superior are in others. Open: the year of the rename to Bacalhôa Vinhos de Portugal, 1998 or 2005, and where João Pires & Filhos began in 1922, so the story gives neither; the soil, sandy loam on the Portuguese sheets and limestone on one English sheet. The principal shareholder from 1998, the American buyer's grandson and the head of João Pires who planted the vines are listed in people.json, the last two as precautions.

picks.why: A family house at Fernando Pó on the sandy plain of Palmela, dating from 1920, whose line has passed through the women of the family and which sold its wine in bulk, for others to bottle, for almost eighty years, until the fourth generation took it in hand in the late 1990s and turned it to bottles under its own labels. The Dona Ermelinda range is named for the third, and its Reserva red, DOC Palmela, keeps Castelão at the heart of a blend with Touriga Nacional, Trincadeira and Cabernet Sauvignon, fermented in stainless steel lagares and aged about a year in French oak half barrels.
picks.note: Answered: 1920 is borne out by Marketeer, Forbes Portugal and Correio da Manhã beside the house; the Reserva is taught as the more widely listed label, its name holding the plan's words, DOC Palmela by Auchan and Continente, and a plain Dona Ermelinda Palmela red is listed beside it; the grapes are the house's own blog, shifting by vintage; the Grande Reserva and the white Reserva are in others. The why's built its name on Castelão is set right as Castelão at the heart of the Reserva; old vines are dropped, found only on two merchants' sheets that read alike. Open: the founder's name, Deonilde or Leonilde, so no early woman is named; the first wine bottled at the house, 1997 or about 2000, the record saying the late 1990s; the appellation of the latest vintages, DOC Palmela or Península de Setúbal. The living family and the house's winemaker are never named and are listed in people.json.

picks.why: A family house at Quinta do Anjo, in the municipality of Palmela, dating from 1910 by its own account and run by three generations of the family, which by its own account backed Moscatel Roxo when the vine had all but disappeared from the region; the press read credits the vine's survival to Bacalhôa and José Maria da Fonseca, so the revival stands as the house's claim. Its Moscatel Roxo, from a pink skinned Muscat thought to be a mutation of Moscatel Galego Branco and at least 85 per cent of the must under DO Setúbal, is fortified, left about five months on its skins and finished in used French oak barrels of 225 litres.
picks.note: Answered, with a correction to the why: credited with bringing back Moscatel Roxo overstated it, the claim being the house's own. 1910 rests on the house's pages and two merchants; the label is Moscatel Roxo under DO Setúbal, Moscatel Roxo de Setúbal being the designation's own name under Portaria 118/2014, vintage dated in some bottlings and not in others; the 85 per cent rule stands in Decreto-Lei 13/92 and is restated by Portaria 118/2014; the serving temperatures are the CVR Península de Setúbal's; the ten year Superior and the Excellent are in others. Open: some merchants list the plain bottling as Heritage Moscatel Roxo; seven months on the skins on some listings, which may belong to the Excellent. The founder is described, his dates not found, and the living family is never named.

picks.why: The Cooperativa Agrícola de Santo Isidro de Pegões, in the municipality of Montijo, chartered on 7 March 1958 to take in and make the grapes of the settler families of the agricultural colony that the state's Junta de Colonização Interna built on the Pegões plain in the 1950s. Trading as Adega de Pegões, it makes its Colheita Seleccionada red and white, and the white taught here, a Vinho Regional Península de Setúbal, is a shifting blend of Verdelho, Antão Vaz, Arinto and Chardonnay with Fernão Pires in many years, fermented in 225 litre oak barrels and rested three to four months on its fine lees.
picks.note: Answered, with a correction to the note: the white is taught, its blend shifting by vintage and lacking Fernão Pires in some (the 2019 sheet, a merchant's 2022), so the five grapes of one sheet are no fixed blend; the full name and the charter of 7 March 1958 are borne out by Infovini and Continente's producer page beside the co-operative's own; the red, whose grapes change by vintage, and the Moscatel de Setúbal are in others. The why's everyday voice of the peninsula was never tested and is dropped. Open: the red's grapes; the trade of the benefactor who gave the Herdade de Pegões to Lisbon's civil hospitals, a brewer by the co-operative and one merchant, a landowner in the accounts the refuter read, so the record says landowner and benefactor and does not name him, his dates not found. The winemaker named by merchants is living and never named.

picks.why: The estate by Casa Branca of the Reynolds family, who came to the Alentejo for cork, their forebear moving there around 1832 by the house's account; the family is thought to have brought the first Alicante Bouschet vines from France in the nineteenth century, the winery with its stone lagares came in 1901, the first bottling in 1949 and the Mouchão label with the harvest of 1954, and after the expropriation that followed 1974 the estate came back to the family, in 1986 by its own account. Mouchão, Alicante Bouschet in the great majority with Trincadeira, from the Carrapetos vineyard planted in 1988, is trodden by foot in those lagares and rested about three years in large wooden tonéis, and its tannin carries it for decades.
picks.note: Answered, with a correction to the why: made only in accepted years is not borne out, no source naming a year without a Mouchão red, while the house keeps that rule for Tonel 3 and 4, which is in others with Dom Rafael; Alicante Bouschet planted since the nineteenth century is the grape's coming to the estate, not the flagship's vines, which grow in the Carrapetos vineyard of 1988. No member of the family is named, no two sources giving any one's dates; the restorers of 1986 and their son are listed in people.json, the first two as precautions. Open: the year of the return, 1986 by the house and 1985 by two others; the forebear's coming, around 1832 by the house, while one account has him in Portugal from 1820 and settled at Estremoz in 1850; Tonel 3 and 4's years in cask and bottle.

picks.why: The private charitable foundation of Évora set up in 1963 by Vasco Maria Eugénio de Almeida (1913 to 1975), an agronomist who had restored the Carthusian monastery of Santa Maria Scala Coeli, to which monks returned in 1960; its wines are made at the Cartuxa winery, named for them. The Pêra-Manca name, older than the wine and offered to the foundation in the late 1980s by an heir of an old farming house of Évora, has marked its red since the first vintage of 1990, bottled only in years the house judges fit: Aragonez and Trincadeira from vines over thirty years, fermented in large French oak vats, aged eighteen months in casks of three thousand litres and some four years in bottle.
picks.note: Answered: the founder is named with his dates from the foundation's page and a second account; the first red of 1990 is borne out by Público and a second account; the voyage of 1500 is told as legend; the Cartuxa Reserva, first made in 1987, is in others. The why's beside the monastery is not said in the record and is dropped. Open: the year the name was ceded, 1987 by Público and two more accounts and 1989 by one, so the record keeps the late 1980s; the monastery's date, 1587 or 1598 on the house's own sheets, and the monks' departure in 2019, both left out. The heir who ceded the name is listed in people.json as a precaution; the foundation's winemaking team is never named.

picks.why: The estate by Reguengos de Monsaraz whose bounds, by its own account, were fixed in 1267 and which the Counts of Alcáçovas held until 1973, when two partners bought it to make wine; occupied in the land reform after April 1974, it gave its first wine only with the harvest of 1985, Esporão Reserva red, and with it began the custom of a different artist's work on each vintage's label. The Reserva blends Alicante Bouschet, Aragonez, Trincadeira and Cabernet Sauvignon, with Touriga Nacional and Syrah in some later vintages, each grape fermented apart and the blend aged twelve months in American and French oak.
picks.note: Answered: the purchase of 1973 and the first Reserva of 1985 are borne out by independent accounts; the grapes are in words and by vintage; the white Reserva and the Private Selection of 2000 are in others. The why's winery of the 1980s that led the Alentejo's modern revival is not said in the record and is dropped, as is one of the region's widely known wines, never tested. Open: the appellation, merchants listing DOC Alentejo while the house's sheets read did not say, so the field stays Alentejo; the year the estate came back after the occupation, 1978 by one account; the painter of the first label of 1985. The two founding partners and the founder's son are never named and are listed in people.json, the second partner as a precaution, as is the long serving winemaker.

picks.why: The co-operative of the growers of Borba, whose first board took office in 1955, on 30 April by its own account, the first of a series of Alentejo co-operative wineries set up with the support of the Junta Nacional do Vinho. Its Reserva red, dressed since its vintage of 1964 in a label of cork and known by it as the Rótulo de Cortiça, is made only in years the co-operative judges exceptional, the 2018 its twenty fifth edition: Aragonez, Trincadeira, Castelão and Alicante Bouschet, DOC Alentejo of the Borba sub-region, aged twelve months in used French oak and casks of exotic wood.
picks.note: Answered: 1955 and the cork label of 1964 are borne out by two independent accounts; the grapes are the house's four; the Grande Reserva and the white Reserva under the cork label are in others. The why's taught a generation of Portuguese what an Alentejo red tastes like is unsourced, the author and the refuter finding it nowhere, and is dropped, as is the marble country, also unsourced; the region record's producers line says the same and is reported in the refuter's file for its editor. Open: the day of the founding, 24 April, 30 April or 7 May 1955; a five litre Reserva without Castelão on one merchant. The winemaker who signs a recent Reserva is listed in people.json; the co-operative's chief executive is never named.

picks.why: The farm near Vidigueira that a Danish and American couple, come to Portugal by sailing boat, found in 1988 and planted with vines in 1991, Syrah among them, when the grape was not allowed in the Alentejo. With the vintage of 1998 the Syrah was bottled on its own and, since its grape could not be named, went out as Incógnito, a Vinho Regional Alentejano; Syrah was later admitted. Its later vintages, a quarter to a half whole bunches and aged in used oak of 500 litres, are lower in alcohol and lighter in frame than the early ones.
picks.note: Answered in part: 1998 is borne out, the record teaching it as the first vintage rather than a year of release; the year Syrah was admitted is not settled (2002 by two accounts, the late 1990s by one, a year after the first Incógnito by another), so the record says later; the label is Vinho Regional Alentejano, one account saying the first vintage could be sold only as a table wine; Cortes de Cima Tinto and Chaminé are in others. Open: the gold medal of the first vintage in Brussels, the house's alone; the grape spelt in an acrostic on the first back label, one account, not carried. The founders and their daughter, who took the estate on in 2019, are never named and are listed in people.json as precautions.

swaps.why: the house's Hardtberg Grosses Gewächs is Frühburgunder, not Spätburgunder; its Spätburgunder GGs come from other sites, and the Hardtberg Spätburgunder GG is Jean Stodden's; house and key kept

picks.why: Dernau family estate on the valley's steep slate and greywacke, its present shape and double name of 1950; Werner Näkel (1953 to 2025) took it on in 1982 and through the 1980s turned it to dry Spätburgunder long on its skins and aged in small oak, and the Pfarrwingert, a VDP Grosse Lage of greywacke and slate at Dernau, gives its Grosses Gewächs.
picks.note: Answered: the year of 1950 and the double name are in two accounts, founded left empty since the family counts more generations at Dernau; Werner Näkel is named with his dates now that he has died, his takeover of 1982 in two sources; the label prints both Dernauer and Dernau Pfarrwingert by year; the Walporzheimer Kräuterberg GG is in others. Open: the first dry barrique vintage, 1987 in two accounts, the record keeping the 1980s. His two daughters, who run the estate, are listed in people.json and never named.

picks.why: Rech family estate of the middle valley, winegrowing there since 1578 and its own wine since 1900 by its own account, calling itself Das Rotweingut and a VDP member since 2005; the Herrenberg beneath the Schwedenkopf rock, the one Grosse Lage of Rech, gives its Spätburgunder Grosses Gewächs from old, often ungrafted vines.
picks.note: Answered: founded stays empty, 1578 and 1900 told as the house's own dates; the site's slate and greywacke follow the VDP's text, which its own table contradicts on height and soil; the making, about three weeks on the skins and about nineteen months in new barriques, is the house's page alone. The Dernauer Hardtberg Spätburgunder in others carries no rank, the house's list and Falstaff disagreeing. The head of the house and his father are listed in people.json and never named.

picks.why: Ahrweiler family estate that holds the whole of the Gärkammer at Walporzheim, by its own account since the early eighteenth century; a small walled terrace of greywacke and slate planted to Spätburgunder alone, which the family calls the smallest Grosse Lage in Germany and the VDP's site page the smallest of the Ahr, named, the VDP says, for the heat its dark rock and walls store.
picks.note: Set right: the smallest in Germany is the family's claim, quoted on the VDP's estate page, not the VDP's own ruling, whose site page says the smallest of the Ahr; no size is printed (0.64 or 0.68 hectare). The label prints Walporzheimer or Walporzheim Gärkammer by year; the making of the Gärkammer itself is in no source found, so the record says only used French barriques, as the VDP described the cellar in 2020. The two co-owners and the younger generation are listed in people.json and never named.

picks.why: Mayschoss estate of the upper valley whose family, the Cossmanns, count their winegrowing from a grower in a castle register of 1574; it left the village cooperative in 1952, was built anew and named Deutzerhof in 1980, and the Mönchberg above it, the Ahr's largest Grosse Lage by the VDP, gives its Spätburgunder Grosses Gewächs.
picks.note: Answered: 1574 is the first record of a family grower, by the house and wein.plus, so founded stays empty; the largest holder of the Mönchberg found no second source and is left out; the handover of 2020 to a friend of the house is history, told with no name. Open: wild yeast fermentation since the 1980s rests on the house's account. The buyer of 2020, the daughter of the house and the cellar master are listed in people.json and never named.

picks.why: Dernau family estate of 1953, a VDP member since 2000, known for Spätburgunder and Frühburgunder; its Grosses Gewächs from the Hardtberg at Dernau is Frühburgunder, the Ahr's early ripening Pinot, so the group shows the valley's own grape beside the Spätburgunder of the other four.
picks.note: Swap of the wine agreed: the house's own pages, wein.plus and Falstaff show its Hardtberg Grosses Gewächs as Frühburgunder only, its Spätburgunder GGs coming from other sites, and the Hardtberg Spätburgunder GG that Falstaff lists is Jean Stodden's; key and house kept. 1953 is in two sources. The Mayschoss cooperative of 1868 is the one the German Wine Institute calls the first wine growers' cooperative, a story for Deutzerhof's record. Open: which generation took over in 1994. The head of the house and the next generation are listed in people.json and never named.

picks.why: Oberhausen family estate whose family came to the village around 1750 by the usual account, its records as growers dating from 1761 by wein.plus; built up parcel by parcel from 1971, it holds plots in the Hermannshöhle at Niederhausen, the site the VDP calls the Nahe's reference for over a century, whose dry Grosses Gewächs the library also teaches as a wine of its own.
picks.note: Answered: the record is tied to p-donnhoff beside w-hermannshohle; 1750 and 1761 are both told; the Hermannshöhle's black grey slate with volcanic rock and its south to south west aspect are the VDP's and the house's; the sweet Oberhäuser Brücke is in others. The why's carried the Nahe onto lists abroad was never tested and is dropped. Open: the year of the Hermannshöhle purchase from a former VDP head on the Nahe. The father and son of 1971, the generation of 2007 and that seller are listed in people.json and never named.

picks.why: Monzingen family estate of the upper Nahe, its vines there since the middle of the eighteenth century and a pure wine estate by 1985, admitted to the VDP in 1994; the Halenberg, a steep slope of blue grey slate and quartzite east of the village that the house recovered from scrub, gives its Grosses Gewächs, with the Frühlingsplätzchen beside it.
picks.note: Answered: the Halenberg's soils are the VDP's on two pages and its aspect is south to south west; the label's form holds; the Halenberg Auslese goes in others. Open: the vessels and the time on lees of the GG, unsourced and left out. The father and son who made it a wine estate are listed in people.json and never named.

picks.why: Bockenau family estate in the Ellerbach valley off the Nahe, admitted to the VDP in 2001, fermenting with wild yeasts into a smoky, struck match style since a new generation took the cellar in 1995; the Felseneck above the village, held by the house alone, gives its Grosses Gewächs.
picks.note: Answered: the upper Nahe is dropped, no source placing the Ellerbach valley there; the Felseneck's slate, quartzite and basalt are named where the VDP and wein.plus agree, its height and aspect the VDP's; the Kupfergrube goes in others. Open: the family's first records, 1780 or 1800, so founded stays empty. The head of the house and his parents are listed in people.json and never named.

picks.why: Niederhausen estate founded by the Prussian state in 1902 as its royal wine domain on the Nahe, on steep rocky ground that took in a copper mine worked until 1901; a state domain until 1998 and named Gut Hermannsberg after its sale in 2009, it holds the Kupfergrube, planted on the old mine, whose Grosses Gewächs it releases at about five years old.
picks.note: Answered: 1902 and the mine to 1901 are the house's and wein.plus's; the year the domain passed to Rhineland-Palatinate is told only as after the Second World War, one account giving 1946 and the house 1950; the sale of 2009 is history with no living name; the holding back is told as a habit begun in the middle 2010s. Open: 1901 for the founding in one summary. The buyers of 2009 are listed in people.json and never named.

picks.why: Burg Layen family estate of the lower Nahe, bought with its castle by a forebear of the Diels in 1802 and admitted to the VDP in 1989, known for Riesling from Dorsheim's Goldloch, Pittermännchen and Burgberg and for traditional method Sekt; the Goldloch, pebbly loam over Permian conglomerate, gives the Grosses Gewächs taught here.
picks.note: Answered, the swap refused: no source ranks the Goldloch GG or the Pittermännchen GG above the other, the house presenting its three Dorsheim GGs as equals, so the plan's Goldloch stands with the Pittermännchen first in others; the Goldloch Sekt is in the story. Open: the buyer of 1802, Johann Peter Diel (1750 to 1811) by wein.plus alone, so the story keeps a forebear. No living Diel met a source by name.

picks.why: Flörsheim-Dalsheim family estate of the Wonnegau, of 1789 by the house's count and the library's date, whose dry Rieslings from limestone changed how Rheinhessen was seen; G-Max, first made with the 2001 vintage, is its dry Riesling from old vines whose parcels the house keeps secret, a wine the library holds on its own.
picks.note: Answered: the record is tied to p-keller beside w-g-max; the first G-Max of 2001 and the name, for a great grandfather Georg who first bottled in 1921 and a son named Max, rest on several accounts; the single Fuder cask was one critic's report and is cut. Open: whether Max is the elder or younger son, and the theft from the Hubacker as the reason for the secret parcels. The library's w-g-max trap calls Georg a grandfather and names two living people, reported for the integrator. The head of the house, his father and his son are listed in people.json and never named.

picks.why: Westhofen family estate with records as growers from 1663, organic by its own account from 1990 and biodynamic from 2004; the Morstein, clay marl over limestone in the Wonnegau, recorded since 1282, gives its Grosses Gewächs, the same hill Keller also bottles, read in a rounder house style.
picks.note: Answered: the label holds as the plan writes it; the biodynamic turn of 2004 is in two sources, the organic start 1990 by the house and the end of the 1980s by the VDP; Kirchspiel, Brunnenhäuschen and Aulerde are in others. The cellar is the house's sheet, most wines in old oak; parcel to a cask was in nothing read and is cut. The head of the house is listed in people.json and never named.

picks.why: Nackenheim estate of 1890, when a banker of Mainz of the Gunderloch family bought Rothenberg vineyards and a manor house; tied by the usual account to Carl Zuckmayer's comedy of 1925, it holds the Rothenberg, the steep red slate of the Roter Hang above the Rhine, which gives its dry Grosses Gewächs and sweet wines up to Trockenbeerenauslese.
picks.note: Answered: 1890 is the house's and two more accounts; the label's form holds; the Rothenberg Trockenbeerenauslese is in others. The making is the house's page, slow natural fermentation in oak and steel and long lees; the cask sizes of trade accounts are cut. Open: the founder's dates, in one source only, so he is described. The owner and his family of today are listed in people.json and never named.

picks.why: Bodenheim family estate with vines in five villages of the Rheinterrasse, its double name from a marriage of 1970 by wein.plus, working the Roter Hang's Pettenthal, Hipping, Ölberg and Rothenberg; its Grosses Gewächs from the Pettenthal at Nierstein shows the red slope's smoky, stony Riesling, the Rothenberg wurzelecht first among its others.
picks.note: The swap to the Rothenberg wurzelecht was proposed by the author and refused by the refuter: the house gives each Grosse Lage its own page and nothing read sets the wurzelecht above the Pettenthal, and the Pettenthal keeps a third Roter Hang site in the group beside Gunderloch's Rothenberg; the plan stands. The ungrafted vines of 1934 were spared the land consolidation by the house's account, nothing more. The estate's shared work with Battenfeld-Spanier is told with no names; the daughter of the house, her husband and the Gillot of 1970 are listed in people.json.

picks.why: Hohen-Sülzen estate in the far south of the Wonnegau, founded in 1991 by its own fact sheets, organic from the start and biodynamic from 2005, on limestone; its Grosses Gewächs from the Frauenberg, a windswept limestone ridge at Nieder-Flörsheim, is the cool, chalky side of the region.
picks.note: Answered: the house gives its three GGs equal pages, so the plan's Frauenberg stands; the Zellerweg am Schwarzen Herrgott lies at Mölsheim on the Rheinhessen side of the border by the VDP, separate from the Schwarzer Herrgott of the Zellertal in the Pfalz, and goes in others with the Kirchenstück. Open: 1991 against 1998 in wein.plus and one profile; the joining with a Battenfeld estate rests on wein.plus alone. The founder and his wife are listed in people.json and never named.

picks.why: Escherndorf family estate above a bend of the Main, its own label young beside the family's long years on the Lump, admitted to the VDP in 2001; its dry Silvaner Grosses Gewächs comes from Am Lumpen 1655, the steep, south facing heart of the Lump on shell limestone, and teaches the grape that defines the region.
picks.note: Answered: the label prints Am Lumpen 1655, the VDP's Grosse Lage at the heart of the Lump, where the library still writes Escherndorfer Lump; the VDP dates the field name to a description of goods and statutes of 1655, which the record follows. Weingut Rainer Sauer, a separate Escherndorf house with a wine of the same name, is kept apart in a trap; the Lump Trockenbeerenauslese is in others. Open: the Hütte planted in 1971 rests on the house's page alone. The founder's daughter and the family are listed in people.json and never named; Horst Sauer and Rainer Sauer stay as the houses' names.

picks.why: Würzburg charitable foundation of 1576, laid down by Prince Bishop Julius Echter von Mespelbrunn (1545 to 1617), whose farms, forests and vineyards were given to pay for its hospital; its Silvaner Grosses Gewächs comes from the Stein, the shell limestone hill above the city that gave Steinwein its name, labelled Stein-Berg from about the 2019 vintage.
picks.note: Answered: 1576 and the founder with his dates are in the foundation's history and Wines of Germany; the Stein, not the Iphöfer Julius-Echter-Berg, is the lead Silvaner, the Julius-Echter-Berg in others. The site's figures are the VDP's for the Stein-Berg. Open: the day of the foundation stone, 12 March in the foundation's history and 12 May in Wines of Germany, so the record gives the year in prose; the Stein-Berg's aspect was not read.

picks.why: Würzburg charitable foundation of 1316, the older of the city's two, given by a patrician and his wife; the Stein-Harfe, a Grosse Lage within the Stein in its sole ownership, gives its Silvaner Grosses Gewächs, while its Stein-Harfe Rieslings are sweet, and its Steinwein of 1718 was sealed in the Bocksbeutel by the city's decree of 1726.
picks.note: Answered: 1316 and the patrician couple in two sources, the founders described, not named, their dates in one source alone; the Stein-Harfe in sole ownership on the house's pages and the VDP's; the sweet Stein-Harfe Riesling Spätlese is in others. The harp etymology and the name Harpfe were not found and are not told. The making follows the house's sheet of 2024, a sheet of 2016 giving steel, so the method is not timeless.

picks.why: Bürgstadt family estate of the Mainviereck on iron rich red sandstone, the red side of Franken, winegrowers there since 1638 by its own history; the Hundsrück, entered again in Franken's official register of vineyards in 2010 after the law of 1971 had folded it into the Centgrafenberg, is the Grosse Lage the house calls its flagship site.
picks.note: Answered: the house's own pages call the Hundsrück its flagship site, so it leads over the Centgrafenberg, which is in others with the Frühburgunder; the return of 2010 was the official register's, not the VDP's. The house's namesake is not dated. Open: when the Hundsrück was first bottled alone, not found; the house cites a document of 1525, the record keeping the VDP's tax record of 1564. The family's living members are listed in people.json and never named.

picks.why: The princely Castell estate on the western edge of the Steigerwald, on gypsum Keuper; the Schlossberg below the castle, held by the estate alone, gives its Silvaner Grosses Gewächs, and the house tells of the first Silvaner recorded in Germany, set at the foot of that hill on 6 April 1659.
picks.note: Answered: the planting of 6 April 1659 is the house's archive, borne out by Wines of Germany and told as the house's account (Wikipedia gives 5 April); the Schlossberg is held alone; the house writes its name Fürstlich Castell'sches Domänenamt. The family's history runs from a presumed ancestor of 1057, with no living name. Open: the house's five years in the castle cellar before release, one sheet only and not told.

picks.why: Schwaigern estate of the counts of Neipperg, whose own tradition holds that the family brought Lemberger to Württemberg in the eighteenth century; the Ruthe, held by the house whole on Gipskeuper of the Heuchelberg, is the Grosse Lage of its Lemberger Grosses Gewächs, with the Schlossberg beside it.
picks.note: Answered: the family's counts are dated (1726, 1821) in two sources; the tie to Saint-Émilion is told as the purchase of 1971 by a branch of the family, with no living name; the Lemberger tradition is told as the house's, not a record; the Ruthe Riesling is in others below Grosses Gewächs, not as a GG. The heads of the family are listed in people.json and never named.

picks.why: Fellbach family estate on the edge of Stuttgart that dates its vines to an ancestor of 1492; its Riesling Grosses Gewächs from Gips Marienglas, the site at Untertürkheim on gypsum Keuper that the family bought in 1973 and calls its flagship site, shows the white side of a red region.
picks.note: Answered: Marienglas names the clear crystal of gypsum; the label reads Untertürkheimer Gips Marienglas. The swap to the Fellbacher Lämmler Lemberger GG was proposed by the author and refused by the refuter: the house's own page calls the Gips its flagship site and no two sources lead with the Lämmler Lemberger, which stays in others; the plan stands. The VDP's figures for its separate Gips page are not this site's and are not given. The family's living members, and the head of 1955 whose status is unknown, are listed in people.json and never named.

picks.why: Fellbach grower's estate of 1997, its own bottles out from 1998, built on Spätburgunder and Lemberger from the Keuper of the Kappelberg; its Spätburgunder Grosses Gewächs comes from old vines in the Brenner, a parcel within the Lämmler, Fellbach's Grosse Lage.
picks.note: Answered: the Lämmler Spätburgunder GG is in the VDP's and Decanter's listings; 1997 is the house's, the VDP's and two others' (one directory 1996); the founder is said, never named, and is listed in people.json. The teacher of 1858 is cut, the year kept as the founding of the Fellbach co-operative. Open: Hans Schnaitmann of 1550 rests on the house's page alone, told as its account.

picks.why: Bönnigheim family estate that dates its vines there to 1510, its leading reds raised in small oak since 1985 by its own account; its Lemberger Grosses Gewächs comes from the Michaelsberg at Cleebronn, the lone hill of the Zabergäu crowned by a Romanesque church, the label printing Cleebronner Michaelsberg.
picks.note: Answered: the VDP's Michaelsberg page and the listings bear out the Lemberger GG, first with the 2010 vintage, the label printing Cleebronner Michaelsberg and earlier bottlings St. Michaelsfeder; no swap was needed. The son's takeover of 2013 and Kreation of 1990 are cut, unsourced. Open: 1985 for the barriques is the house's account. The father and son are listed in people.json and never named.

picks.why: Remstal estate at Stetten east of Stuttgart, begun by its namesake in 1949 and carried on by his son from 1968 and his grandson from 2014; its Riesling Grosses Gewächs from the Pulvermächer, an old terraced slope of Keuper sandstone below the Yburg ruin, shows the Rems valley's white side.
picks.note: Answered: Falstaff and the house's sheets list the Stettener Pulvermächer Riesling GG; the soil is the VDP's, lean sandstone and coloured marl of the Keuper; the name is the VDP's reading, an old word for a blaster of the neighbouring quarry. The founder's dates were not found in two sources, so none is given. Open: the VDP gives two height ranges, the record saying about 330 to 370 metres. The family's living members are listed in people.json and never named.

picks.why: Malterdingen family estate of the Breisgau, of 1987 when the founder left the cooperative to bottle the family's wine, his Spätburgunder made in the manner of Burgundy on limestone; the Bienenberg, where by the VDP's account Cistercian monks grew Spätburgunder in the fourteenth century, is the Grosse Lage of its Grosses Gewächs.
picks.note: Answered: 1987 in the library, Decanter and wein.plus; the founder's death in June 2014 at fifty five with Decanter, his birth year not found in two sources, so he stays undated; his heirs are listed in people.json and never named. Wildenstein is a Grosse Lage of its own in the VDP's list, its GG in others. Malterdinger as an old local name for Pinot Noir is not told. Open: the barrel time rests on importers' sheets.

picks.why: Ihringen family estate of the Kaiserstuhl, begun in 1935 by a country doctor and built up by his son; the Häusleboden, a parcel in the Wanne of the Winklerberg named for the family's vineyard hut, on volcanic rock, gives its Spätburgunder Grosses Gewächs.
picks.note: Answered: 1935 and the doctor are the house's and the VDP's; the label prints Winklerberg Häusleboden and Winklerberg Wanne Häusleboden by year; the Grauburgunder of the hill is no longer claimed in the why, unsourced in the record. The walled terraces and the doctor's wartime recall were not found and are cut. Open: the élevage is Falstaff's for 2020 alone. The family's living members, and the doctor's son whose status is unsettled, are listed in people.json and never named.

picks.why: Oberbergen family estate of the Kaiserstuhl, tied to the Schwarzer Adler, whose kitchen won its first Michelin star in 1969, and by its own account taking its lead from the dry wines of France across the Rhine; its Grauburgunder Grosses Gewächs from the Schlossberg at Achkarren shows the region's white Pinot.
picks.note: Answered: the VDP's Schlossberg page lists the Achkarrer Schlossberg as a Grosse Lage for the house and Falstaff lists the GG over many vintages, so the merge read's condition holds and the pick stands. Franz Keller the elder is named with his dates (1927 to 2007); the estate joined the VDP in 2014. Founded stays empty: the house gives 1892 and the turn of the century. The present head and his son are listed in people.json and never named.

picks.why: Neuweier estate by Baden-Baden in the Ortenau, Riesling planted in 1785 by the castle's lord by local accounts; its Mauerberg Riesling goes into the Bocksbeutel, the flask otherwise kept for Franken, by an old right whose origin the accounts tell two ways.
picks.note: Answered: the VDP names the Grosse Lage Mauerberg Mauerwein; the lord of 1785 stays undescribed by name, his dates resting on wein.plus alone; the sale of 2012 is told with no living name. Neuweier and a few neighbouring villages of the Rebland are among the few places outside Franken that may use the Bocksbeutel; no closed list is given, the Weinverordnung itself not read. Open: the cellar's vessels, accounts differing. The owner and an earlier figure of the estate are listed in people.json and never named.

picks.why: Efringen-Kirchen family estate of the Markgräflerland near Basel, founded by a couple of the village in 1991 or 1992, outside the VDP and bottling much of its range as Landwein; Jaspis 10hoch4 is its Gutedel, the Markgräflerland's own grape, from old vines on limestone and long on its lees in wood.
picks.note: Answered: Falstaff lists Jaspis 10hoch4 Gutedel and later 10hoch4 Gutedel, one wine under two labels, told in a trap; the founder is said, never named, and listed in people.json. Open: what 10hoch4 means, unsettled, so not told; why the house bottles as Landwein, not told; no primary source was reached, every fact resting on two secondary ones; the cask size is not claimed.

swaps.why: the VDP ranks only Im Hahn, the core of the Hahn, Grosse Lage and Falstaff prints Bacharach Im Hahn Riesling GG for the years taught, while the wider Bacharacher Hahn is an Erste Lage; the same wine under its label's name, house and key kept

no label reading Oberweseler Engehöll Riesling was found; Falstaff lists Engehöll Bernstein Am Lauerbaum Riesling GG and the VDP ranks Bernstein Am Lauerbaum Grosse Lage; the same wine under its label's name, house and key kept

picks.why: Bacharach family estate, also called the Hahnenhof, joined in 1953 by marriage with the Weller estate of Walluf in the Rheingau and a VDP member since 1987; its Riesling Grosses Gewächs comes from Im Hahn, the core of the Hahn that the VDP ranks Grosse Lage, on Devonian slate above the Rhine.
picks.note: Answered: the VDP ranks the wider Bacharacher Hahn, the estate's monopole, Erste Lage and its core Im Hahn Grosse Lage, and Falstaff prints Bacharach Im Hahn Riesling GG, so the pick's wine was renamed (the swap above). 1831 is the house's account, and the Walkenberg GG is in others. Open: the stainless steel rests on Falstaff's listings alone. The family is listed in people.json and never named.

picks.why: Steeg family estate in a side valley at Bacharach, a VDP member since 1987, known also for traditional method Riesling Sekt; its Riesling Grosses Gewächs comes from the St. Jost, a Grosse Lage of Devonian slate under windblown sand of volcanic origin.
picks.note: Answered: the St. Jost's figures and its windblown sand are the VDP's; the Sekt and the stainless steel stand on two sources; the Wolfshöhle GG is in others. The three hundred years were the building's, not the family's, and are cut; founded stays empty. The father who chaired the VDP Mittelrhein from 1998 to 2010 and the son are listed in people.json and never named.

picks.why: Spay family estate in the Bopparder Hamm, the long loop of the Rhine at Boppard, a VDP member since 2007; its Riesling Grosses Gewächs comes from the Mandelstein, slate facing south south east, from the house's oldest parcel there, with the Feuerlay GG beside it.
picks.note: Answered: the Mandelstein leads by the house's own words and the VDP's page gives the site; the Feuerlay and An der Rabenlei GGs are in others. The estate carries a living grower's name: Matthias Müller stays as the house's name and is not listed in people.json, since the Weingart record names the house too; the family is said, never named, and the rest of it is listed.

picks.why: Spay family estate outside the VDP, turned wholly to wine in the 1960s and run by the son of the house since 1996, labelling its Riesling of the Bopparder Hamm by the Prädikat; the Feuerlay, south facing slate under loess loam, is the site it is known by, its Spätlese trocken the dry wine taught.
picks.note: Answered: the Prädikat is Spätlese trocken; the Feuerlay's figures are the VDP's; the Engelstein and the Ohlenberg are in others. Open: standing outside the VDP is a present state that has held for the life of its labels; the integrator may word it as history. The family is listed in people.json and never named.

picks.wine: Engehöll Bernstein Am Lauerbaum Riesling GG
picks.why: Oberwesel family estate of the slate gorge, enlarged by a new generation from 1991 and admitted to the VDP in 1995; its Riesling Grosses Gewächs comes from Am Lauerbaum, the Grosse Lage within the Engehöller Bernstein, a south facing hollow of Devonian slate, with the Oelsberg GG beside it.
picks.note: Answered: no label reading Oberweseler Engehöll Riesling was found, and the wine is the Engehöll Bernstein Am Lauerbaum GG Falstaff lists, so the pick was renamed (the swap above); the site's figures are the VDP's; the Oelsberg GG is in others. The new generation is listed in people.json and never named.

swaps.why: the Nussberg is a hill of several Rieden and no label reads Ried Nussberg; the house's sheets print Ried Ulm 1ÖTW Nussberg Wiener Gemischter Satz DAC; house and key kept
the house and Falstaff print Riesling Nussberg Weißer Marmor with no Ried; house and key kept

picks.wine: Ried Ulm Nussberg Wiener Gemischter Satz
picks.why: Stammersdorf family estate on the Bisamberg side of the Danube with vines on the Nussberg, biodynamic since 2008 and a founder of WienWein in 2006, which argued for the city's field blend as a fine wine; its Gemischter Satz from Ried Ulm, an Erste Lage of the Nussberg on shell limestone, is that blend from one Ried.
picks.note: Answered: the Nussberg is a hill of several Rieden and the label prints Ried Ulm, so the pick was renamed (the swap above); WienWein of 2006 and the DAC of the 2013 vintage are on two sources; the Rosengartel is in others. The library's Ried Nussberg and its Grand Select are listed as Codex records in tension. The head of the house is listed in people.json and never named.

picks.why: Heiligenstadt Heuriger house that has pressed wine since 1683 by its own account, where Ludwig van Beethoven (1770 to 1827) lodged in 1817; Weisser Marmor is its Riesling from the lime rich slopes of the Nussberg, made in steel, beside its field blends from the Preussen and the Langteufel.
picks.note: Answered: the label prints Riesling Nussberg Weisser Marmor with no Ried (the swap above); the stay of May to June 1817 is in Beethoven's letters; the sale is told without a year, since sources give 2006 and 2007, and with no living name. Open: the head of the Mayer family who handed the estate on is not named, his death given as 2011 and 2013.

picks.why: Grinzing estate on the hill named for Count Johann Philipp Cobenzl (1741 to 1810), who took it in 1773, bought by the City of Vienna in 1907 and built up as a vineyard from 1988; its Gemischter Satz from the Ried Reisenberg, the hill on which the estate stands, is the city's field blend from one named site.
picks.note: Answered: the house writes Weingut Cobenzl; 1773 and 1907 stand on the estate and the Wien Geschichte Wiki, told as history, never as a present owner; the Steinberg, the Erste Lage, is in others and a trap. Open: one press article gives 1905 for the city's purchase.

picks.why: Jedlersdorf family estate on the Bisamberg, on the Danube's left bank, whose Heuriger began in 1927, a founder of WienWein in 2006 and organic since 2014; its Gemischter Satz from the Wiesthalen, an Erste Lage of the Österreichische Traditionsweingüter, is the left bank's field blend from one site, long in barrel.
picks.note: Answered: the Heuriger of 1927 and its room of 1959 are the house's account; the barrel time is more than a year, since the house gives thirteen and eighteen months. Open: organic from 2014 rests on the house's own timeline. The head of the house is listed in people.json and never named.

picks.why: Mauer family estate with its Heuriger since 1930, a founder of WienWein in 2006 and Demeter certified from 2018, with vines from the Maurerberg to the Nussberg; its Gemischter Satz from the Kaasgraben, a small plot in the 19th district that the house lists under the Nussberg, is a field blend given skin contact and large casks.
picks.note: Answered: the Kaasgraben lies in the 19th district, not in Mauer; the Orangetraube planted alone in 1966 is the house's account and is in others. Open: organic from 2017 and Demeter from 2018 rest on the house and its importer. The family is listed in people.json and never named.

swaps.why: the house names the wine Grüner Veltliner Hund, short for the Hundsleiten, printed in full on earlier labels; no label read prints Ried Hund; house and key kept
the house's own page names its Weinviertel DAC Grüner Veltliner Röschitz, the appellation staying Weinviertel DAC; the same classic tier wine, house and key kept

picks.why: Stetten family estate just north of Vienna, a mixed farm turned to wine by a young couple of the family from 1978; its Grüner Veltliner Hund, named for the Hundsleiten above the village, a slope of flysch the family had long owned, is its Weinviertel DAC Reserve.
picks.note: Answered: the house names the wine Hund, short for the Hundsleiten printed on earlier labels, with no Ried (the swap above); Hommage is in others. Another Weinviertel winery of the family name is kept apart in a trap without its names. Open: the flysch and the eight hours on the skins rest on the house's sheet. The founders and their heirs are listed in people.json and never named.

picks.why: Poysdorf family estate of the north east Weinviertel, taken over by a young couple in the early years of this century, farmed organically and making single Ried Grüner Veltliner and Sekt; the Bürsting, old vines on deep loam beside the Sauberg, is its Grüner Veltliner from one site.
picks.note: Answered: the Bürsting stands as the flagship by the longer record; the swap to the Ried Sauberg 1ÖTW was refused, and the Sauberg and the Hermannschachern are in others. Founded stays empty (2007 against a first vintage of 2006). Open: the appellation on the label, Niederösterreich or Weinviertel DAC Reserve, by the year. The couple are listed in people.json and never named.

picks.why: Schrattenthal family estate near Retz in the far west of the Weinviertel, turned wholly to wine in the 1980s and a founder of the ÖTW's Weinviertel association in 2024; the Äussere Bergen, weathered granite under loess, is its Weinviertel DAC Reserve Grüner Veltliner from one Ried.
picks.note: Answered: the site's soil is granite of the Manhartsberg under loess; the village Riesling is in others. Open: the Äussere Bergen as an ÖTW Erste Lage rests on the house's product name; the share of steel on one note. Father and son are listed in people.json and never named.

picks.why: Hohenwarth family estate on the western edge of the Weinviertel, at work there since 1705 by its own account and a wine estate alone since 2001; 8000 is its Weinviertel DAC Reserve from the chalky Ried Laa, named for its planting of about eight thousand vines to every ten thousand square metres.
picks.note: Answered: the figure is the planting density, by the house; the Große Reserve from the same Ried and the Roter Veltliner Ried Kreimelberg, the house's second flagship, are in others. Open: the Laa as an ÖTW Erste Lage rests on the house's product name. The family is listed in people.json and never named.

picks.why: Röschitz family estate on the eastern slopes of the Manhartsberg, run by three siblings since 2012 and farmed organically; its Grüner Veltliner Röschitz is the Weinviertel DAC in its classic tier, the dry, peppery wine the appellation was made for, from primary rock and granite under loess.
picks.note: Answered: the house names its classic Weinviertel DAC Grüner Veltliner Röschitz (the swap above), so no swap to Weinrieder was needed; the Reipersberg and the Mühlberg are in others. Founded stays empty, since the chamber gives wine growing since 1814 and the family more than two hundred years. Open: some export listings still print Klassik. The siblings are listed in people.json and never named.

swaps.why: the house bottles Schilcher from several Rieden, and the record teaches the one from the Hochgrail, a high slope of gneiss, under the name its label prints; the same house and the same Schilcher, house and key kept

picks.why: Berghausen family estate of the Südsteiermark, begun in 1959 on the Zieregg and the Grassnitzberg, which farms the Slovenian half of the Zieregg as Domaine Ciringa; its Sauvignon Blanc from the Zieregg, a steep slope of coralline limestone above the winery and a Grosse STK Ried, is wild fermented and kept long in large casks.
picks.note: Answered: the Zieregg is coralline limestone with calcareous marl in places, the label Südsteiermark DAC Ried Zieregg GSTK; the Slovenian half is Ciringa, under Štajerska Slovenija. Open: the house among the founders of the Steirische Klassik group of 1986 is hedged as the sources tell it. The family is listed in people.json and never named.

picks.why: Gamlitz family estate around a farmhouse the house dates to 1886, an inn as well as a winery since 1990 and organic since 2013; its Sauvignon Blanc from the Kranachberg, a high, cool ridge between Gamlitz and Leutschach and a Grosse STK Ried, is raised in steel on its lees, with the Sernauberg and the Pfarrweingarten beside it.
picks.note: Answered: the label reads Südsteiermark DAC Ried Kranachberg GSTK; a rename to Ried Alter Kranachberg, the name Falstaff lists from about the 2021 vintage, was weighed and refused by the refuter, and the later name is taught in a trap and in others. Open: the ridge's height and its quartz sands rest on the house's sheet. The family is listed in people.json and never named.

picks.why: Ratsch family estate that dates its winegrowing to 1907 on the Witscheiner Herrenberg, left in Slovenia by the border after the First World War, and bought the Nussberg in 1986; its Sauvignon Blanc from that steep slope of Opok, the local calcareous marl, a Grosse STK Ried, is raised long in large casks and released late.
picks.note: Answered: the soil is Opok and the label Südsteiermark DAC Ried Nussberg GSTK, Ratscher Nussberg in early vintages; a trap keeps it apart from Vienna's Nussberg. Open: the Nussberg's renown since the thirteenth century and the bottle of 1868 rest on the house. The father and his two sons are listed in people.json and never named.

picks.why: Straden family estate of the Vulkanland Steiermark, which took on the Saziani estate around 1970 and has been certified organic since the 2013 vintage; its Sauvignon Blanc from the Moarfeitl, the family's first vineyard and a Grosse STK Ried, grows on limestone sediment over Sarmatian gravel rather than volcanic rock, beside its Saziani Grauburgunder.
picks.note: Answered: the Moarfeitl's soil is calcareous sandy loam over Sarmatian gravel and the label Vulkanland Steiermark DAC Ried Moarfeitl GSTK; the lees time is fourteen to eighteen months by vintage. Open: the 1930s for the Moarfeitl rest on the house's account. The family is listed in people.json and never named.
